title: Coordinator host hardening (the unbuilt half of the ADR-0012 Direction 3 mitigation)
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (both reviewers' FIRST or SECOND attack target). ADR-0012 Direction 3 accepts permanently that a coordinator compromised BEFORE the wrench reads the normal PIN and substitutes it for the duress PIN: the escape never arms, no node locks down, and — because every observable is pin-uniform BY DESIGN — the user sees exactly what a working duress path would show. The coerced spend completes after the Hold. This is the only accepted conditional-THEFT residual in the system.

The ADR names two mitigations: a hardened dedicated host, and reproducible builds. NEITHER EXISTS. Reproducible builds are btc-policy-rel; this bead is the host.

DELIVER: a documented, reproducible coordinator-host build/deploy — minimal base, no ambient network egress beyond what the relay needs, disk encryption, no other tenants, an update story, and an explicit statement of what an attacker who owns this host still gets (which is: the plaintext PIN, hence duress nullification, bounded by allowlist + Hot budget). Pair it with btc-policy-bq6 (hardware signing) so the USER KEY is not also on that host — today it would be, which merges this residual with adversary A3.

BE HONEST ABOUT THE CEILING: hardening reduces the probability of pre-wrench compromise; it does not remove the capability. ADR-0012's Direction 1 (a device-bound PIN the coordinator never sees in plaintext) is the actual fix and is deferred to hardware. This bead must not be written up as closing the residual — say what it buys and what it leaves.

VERIFY: the host build is reproducible and documented end-to-end; a written argument, reviewable by an external auditor, for what compromise of this host still yields.

title: Armed-escape Confirmed branch skips the hot-conflict invalidation scan (k0t follow-up)
description: codex k0t review [P2]. When a confirmed duress escape spends inputs also used by hot candidates OTHER than its paired request, production takes the ArmedEscapeState::Confirmed branch (crates/vault-node/src/lib.rs ~2881), which removes only commitment_id and its paired sibling from state.pending. It never calls channel.mark_broadcast, so the input-overlap invalidation scan (channel.rs ~4470, added by btc-policy-k0t) never runs for those other defeated candidates. They therefore stay in GET /pending until expiry even though the node has already observed the conflicting sweep on-chain — contradicting the endpoint's documented settlement semantics ('an id disappears once the candidate is observed on the network') and leaving their Hot-budget reservations metered. FIX SHAPE: extract the overlap scan + release_if_unexposed + mark from mark_broadcast into a separate method (e.g. invalidate_hot_conflicts(spender_id) -> Vec<String>) that does NOT touch the spender candidate itself, then call it from BOTH mark_broadcast and the Confirmed branch, removing the returned ids from state.pending. CARE REQUIRED — this is why it was not done inline: mark_broadcast takes the channel STORE lock while the Confirmed branch already holds SIGN_STATE, so a naive call introduces a lock-order inversion in crown-jewel fire-path code. Establish and document the ordering (or restructure so the store lock is taken outside the sign_state hold) rather than nesting them by accident. The armed escape itself must still be RETAINED through the fire window for in-window reorg recovery. Gates: fmt/clippy-D/workspace tests, attack 16/16, all 3 demos, plus a test that a confirmed escape clears OTHER conflicting hot candidates from /pending and returns their budget.

title: attack all: a genuinely racing spend/refresh preflight scenario (f91 follow-up)
description: Fable f91 review [P1], recorded rather than silently dropped. btc-policy-f91's acceptance said 'attack all still passes incl. a new spend-refresh-race scenario'. That scenario does NOT exist: crates/vault-cli/src/attack.rs's in_flight_refresh drives the refresh to acceptance on all nodes and WAITS FOR ITS TXID (attack.rs ~4649-4667) before building the coerced spend, so the refresh is fully settled and the out-of-lock preflight window is never raced. SCOPE DECISION for f91: shipped with the race proven at unit level instead — preflight_concurrency::a_refresh_racing_an_in_flight_spend_is_subordinated uses mock-backend barriers to hold a spend inside its preflight window while a refresh runs, and Fable independently verified the ordering argument in code (the refresh's two-half predicate check and its register_pair sit under one continuous sign_state hold, and the spend's marker claim is published under that same lock, so the mutex totally orders them). WHY NOT INLINE: f91's own task file forbade threading flaky live timing through the harness, citing the /healthz over-specification lesson (a fragile end-to-end poll cost ~12h and proved nothing the unit test did not). A live version needs a deliberately stalled backend — a gettxout-delaying proxy, or SIGSTOP on one node's bitcoind while the spend is in flight — which is that same fragile pattern. WHAT THIS BEAD BUYS: the unit test cannot exercise real HTTP handler threading, real lock contention, or a real bitcoind stall, so a scheduling-dependent break of the barrier-verified ordering would go unseen. IF IMPLEMENTED it must be DETERMINISTIC — prefer a proxy that deterministically blocks the gettxout batch until the harness releases it, over sleeps or SIGSTOP timing. title: V0-4a: dual PINs (both-Argon2 constant-time) + attempt budget + Lockdown
description:
## V0-4a: dual Argon2id pins + attempt budget with embedded transition table (terminal backoff explicit; max_attempts>=1 + nonempty backoff_schedule validated), same-shaped mutation, deployment-death reboot. Folded audit r3.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file gitignored):

# V0-4a: dual PINs (both-Argon2 constant-time) + per-node attempt budget + Lockdown

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Node-local, NO channel** — buildable in parallel with V0-8b (does not depend
  on it). Authoritative: `docs/adr/0012-...` (invariants: "Pin-compare is
  constant-cost", "Fail-closed lockout"), `docs/adr/0013-...` §7 (pin-attempt
  budget), `docs/adr/0008-duress-pins-and-lockdown.md` (Lockdown, RAMDISK),
  `CONTEXT.md` (Duress PIN, Lockdown). The config already has
  `pin_normal_hash`/`pin_duress_hash` (currently plain SHA-256 placeholders —
  this task moves them to Argon2id).

## Outcome
The node verifies the per-request PIN against two enrolled Argon2id digests
**without leaking which pin (or wrong-pin) was submitted through timing**, guards
online guessing with a per-node attempt budget, and can enter the terminal
**Lockdown** state. This task builds the pin/lockdown SUBSTRATE (verification +
budget + lockdown state + FRAUD_SUSPECTED refusal); it does NOT build the duress
arming/sweep state machine (that is V0-4b, which consumes this).

## Why this exists
The duress mechanism (V0-4b) is only as silent as its pin comparison. ADR-0012's
final review found that different Argon2 salts + a short-circuit compare make a
duress pin cost one extra Argon2 (~100ms), measurable by a coordinator-attacker.
And a valid duress pin must arm even under wrong-pin lockout (fail-closed). This
task gets those load-bearing timing/lockout semantics right in isolation, so
V0-4b builds duress logic on a sound pin substrate.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node`, config)
### 1. Argon2id pin digests + constant-cost compare (ADR-0012 invariant)
- `pin_normal_hash`/`pin_duress_hash` become **Argon2id PHC strings** (own
  salts). **Validate both at startup** as Argon2id with acceptable parameters
  and DISTINCT salts (fatal config error otherwise).
- **On every `SpendRequest`** (NOT RefreshRequest — codex C2: refresh is
  pin-less, ADR-0013 §2, performs NO pin compare and cannot touch the budget),
  **compute BOTH digests unconditionally and constant-time-select the outcome**
  — normal / duress / wrong-pin all cost exactly two Argon2 evaluations and the
  same work. A short-circuit ("try normal; if match stop") is FORBIDDEN — it
  makes duress cost one extra Argon2. "Constant-time byte-compare of the hash"
  alone is NOT sufficient; both Argon2 evaluations must always run.
- The compare yields an internal enum `{Normal, Duress, Wrong}` via a
  constant-time select. Use a **secret PIN newtype** and **zeroize every owned
  copy** of the pin (request buffers + error paths, not just logs). The pin is
  ephemeral, never logged/persisted anywhere (ADR-0008).

### 2. Per-node attempt budget (ADR-0013 §7) — with a NORMATIVE transition table
- RAMDISK/node-lifetime state (tmpfs reboot-death — not durable; a reboot
  destroys the budget AND the signing key alike, so no reset-by-reboot).
- Config: `pin_attempt_budget { max_attempts, window_secs, backoff_schedule,
  lockout_secs }`. **Implement EXACTLY this normative transition table (codex C1
  — embedded here so two implementations cannot diverge). State: `fails`
  (wrong-pin count in the current `window_secs`), `locked_until` (unix secs).**

  | Current state | Event | Action | Next |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | not locked, `fails = k < max_attempts−1` | wrong pin | `fails += 1`; sleep `backoff_schedule[min(k, len−1)]` | not locked, `fails = k+1` |
  | not locked, `fails = max_attempts−1` | wrong pin (**the `max_attempts`-th**) | **sleep `backoff_schedule[min(max_attempts−1, len−1)]` (the terminal backoff — every wrong pin including this one sleeps first), THEN** `fails = max_attempts`; `locked_until = now + lockout_secs` | **locked** |
  | not locked | correct **normal** pin | no budget change (does NOT reset `fails`) | not locked |
  | not locked | correct **duress** pin | no budget change; invoke arm-hook | not locked |
  | not locked | oldest wrong-pin older than `window_secs` | that failure drops out of `fails` (sliding window) | not locked |
  | **locked** (`now < locked_until`) | ANY SpendRequest (normal/duress/wrong) | refuse to sign; **a wrong pin does NOT extend `locked_until`** (no infinite-extension); **a correct DURESS pin STILL invokes the arm-hook** (fail-closed) | locked |
  | locked, `now ≥ locked_until` | any | `fails = 0`; `locked_until` cleared | not locked |

  So: **every wrong pin sleeps its backoff first**, and the `max_attempts`-th
  one then enters lockout (no off-by-one, and "backoff THEN lockout" is
  consistent between the table and the tests). A wrong-pin flood during lockout
  cannot extend it. **Config validation (fatal at startup):** `max_attempts ≥ 1`
  and `backoff_schedule` non-empty (otherwise `max_attempts−1` / `len−1` are
  undefined). No cross-node accounting (per-node suffices — the pin is the same
  value everywhere).
- **Same-shaped budget work (codex C3 — ADR-0012 checklist):** every
  `SpendRequest` performs the **same lock acquisition and the same-shaped state
  update**, with the logical next budget value chosen by **constant-time
  select** — only the *logical* wrong-count changes, never the observable work
  shape. (Not just "two Argon2 evaluations": the budget mutation must also be
  timing-uniform across normal/duress/wrong.)
- **Lockout ≠ Lockdown**: lockout is a transient rate-limit; a locked-out node
  refuses to sign (denial), then recovers after `lockout_secs`.
- **Fail-closed (ADR-0012 invariant):** a valid **duress** pin is a *matching*
  compare — it does NOT consume the attempt budget and (the arming it triggers,
  built in V0-4b) must fire regardless of lockout state. The budget rate-limits
  ONLY wrong pins. A locked-out node signs nothing, so lockout produces denial,
  never an unfrozen signing quorum. (V0-4a exposes the budget verdict + a hook
  V0-4b uses to arm-even-when-locked-out.)

### 3. Lockdown state (ADR-0008, terminal)
- A node-lifetime **Lockdown** state (RAMDISK — never durable disk; reboot =
  node death is strictly stronger; `/unseal` rejected so no durable flag). While
  in Lockdown, every spend/refresh request → `FRAUD_SUSPECTED`; no reset on
  sealed nodes; the only exit is the recovery path.
- V0-4a builds the STATE + the FRAUD_SUSPECTED refusal + the enter-Lockdown
  entry point; V0-4b drives WHEN it is entered (at T under duress).

## Tests
- **Structural constant-cost (PRIMARY — codex improvement):** an injectable
  verifier asserts EXACTLY two Argon2 evaluations run in a fixed order per
  SpendRequest, and budget instrumentation asserts identical state touches
  (lock + same-shaped update) across normal/duress/wrong. A statistical
  wall-clock latency test is SUPPLEMENTAL (keep it coarse to avoid flaky CI).
- **Attempt budget (per the transition table):** reaching `max_attempts` wrong
  pins within `window_secs` → backoff then lockout; a locked-out node refuses to
  sign; recovers after `lockout_secs`; a correct (normal) pin does NOT consume
  the budget; **a valid NORMAL pin is still refused during lockout while a valid
  DURESS pin still invokes the arm hook** (codex improvement).
- **Fail-closed**: a valid duress pin is a matching compare that does NOT consume
  the budget, and the arm-hook fires even when the node is locked out on
  wrong-pin floods; a pin-less RefreshRequest never mutates the budget.
- **Lockdown**: entering Lockdown → every subsequent spend/refresh →
  FRAUD_SUSPECTED; no reset; the pin is never logged/persisted AND request
  buffers/error paths are zeroized (a secret-newtype + zeroize check, not just a
  log grep).
- **Reboot-death = DEPLOYMENT death (codex C5):** the reboot test must destroy
  the simulated RAMDISK/config (incl. `node_seckey`), then assert the node
  CANNOT restart or rejoin (bare machine) — NOT "restart the same binary against
  the same TOML and return an HTTP refusal" (that resurrects the node). The
  budget + Lockdown are gone with everything else; capacity to sign is gone too.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/` + config + **narrowly-scoped `crates/vault-cli`
  demo/config fixtures** (codex C4 — moving the config pins to Argon2 PHC strings
  requires updating the demo-generated configs/fixtures so `demo first-light`
  still passes). Do NOT build the duress state machine (arming/freeze/sweep/
  Firing — V0-4b), the channel, or broadcast. Do NOT persist the pin or any
  duress signal to durable disk (RAMDISK only).
- **Sequencing:** this rides on V0-8b's final tagged-request shape (both rewrite
  the request handler) — build AFTER V0-8b establishes the stable protocol, then
  attach pin handling to it (codex dependency conclusion).
- Non-goals: device-bound duress tokens (Direction 1/2 rejected), PAKE, pin
  transport hardening (v1). Build the simplest correct substrate.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- Both Argon2 digests always computed + constant-time-selected (timing test
  passes); per-node budget rate-limits wrong pins and never a valid duress pin;
  Lockdown is terminal + RAMDISK + FRAUD_SUSPECTED. The pin substrate is ready
  for V0-4b to build arming/sweep on.

title: V0-8a0: migrate vault-node to tokio+axum, http.rs deleted
description:
## Outcome
vault-node serves /sign + /events via axum on tokio (one port, fully async), with http.rs deleted. Behavior-neutral for what the coordinator consumes. This async base is the prerequisite for the node channel (V0-8a) and every timer-driven milestone after it (V0-8b Hold-expiry combine, V0-4 duress T).

## Why this exists
The hand-rolled synchronous HTTP server (crates/vault-node/src/http.rs) is one sequential serve loop: a stalled client head-of-line-blocks /sign for up to 10s, and it cannot host the peer-facing /channel route or async timers. Migrating while the surface is two routes is far cheaper than after V0-8a/V0-8b/V0-4 pile onto the sync shape (2026-07-16 eng review).

## Verification (ship gate)
nix develop -c cargo fmt --check; clippy -D warnings; cargo test --workspace; demo first-light exits 0. http.rs no longer exists. The new HTTP-level regression tests lock the axum edge contract, and the sign-path atomicity + no-cancel tests prove the concurrency model.

## Deployment context (ADR-0007)
The whole node runs from tmpfs/ramdisk: reboot = bare machine = permanent node death. "State on disk" never means durable; nothing this task writes needs to survive a reboot.

---
FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained executable memory; the rb-lite task file this was transferred from is gitignored):

# V0-8a0: migrate vault-node to tokio + axum — behavior-neutral where it counts, http.rs deleted

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run EVERY cargo/bitcoind command through the flake dev
  shell: `nix develop -c cargo test`, etc. Plain `cargo` fails.
- This is a **mechanical migration**. It exists so the next task (V0-8a, the
  node channel) lands on an async base as a small, security-only diff.
  Decision record (2026-07-16 eng review): the node goes **fully async**
  (tokio + axum), all surfaces on **one port**, because V0-8a adds a
  peer-facing route and V0-8b/V0-4 add timers (Hold-expiry, duress T).
  Deployment context (ADR-0007, informs no code here but explains the state
  model): the whole node runs from **tmpfs/ramdisk** — reboot = bare machine
  = node death. So "state on disk" never means durable; nothing this task
  writes needs to survive a reboot.

## Problem description
`crates/vault-node/src/http.rs` is a hand-rolled synchronous HTTP/1.1 server —
one sequential serve loop, one request at a time. It was right when `/sign` was
the only route; it is wrong as the base for the channel (head-of-line blocking:
a stalled client holds the loop up to 10s) and for the timer-driven milestones
after it. Replace it with axum on tokio.

**Compatibility contract (be precise about what "behavior-neutral" means):**
- **Byte-compatible** for what the coordinator consumes: `POST /sign` → 200
  with the exact signed/pending/refusal JSON; 400 with `{"error": detail}` on
  an undecodable body (`BadRequest` stays 400, never a refusal). `GET /events`
  / `/events?since=<cursor>` → same JSON; absent/unparseable `since` reads 0.
- **Edge statuses adopt axum's standard answers** (oversized body may be 413,
  wrong method 405, unknown route 404 with axum's body, query strings routed by
  path). Do NOT replicate the hand-rolled server's quirks — instead the
  regression tests below CAPTURE the new edge contract so it is explicit and
  locked from now on.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node` + workspace manifests)
1. **Add deps**: `tokio` (rt-multi-thread, macros, time, net) and `axum` to
   vault-node. Workspace-pin versions; `Cargo.lock` changes accordingly.
   Nothing else — no tower-http, no tracing stack, no reqwest (V0-8a adds it).
2. **Port routes to axum** per the compatibility contract above. Body limit
   stays 1 MiB (`DefaultBodyLimit`). Add a request-timeout layer for handler
   execution. A client that stalls mid-headers no longer wedges anything (each
   connection is its own task — that is the point of the migration); a
   socket-level header-read deadline is v1 hardening, NOT this task.
3. **Sign-path atomicity (critical).** Today the sequential serve loop gives
   `handle_sign` end-to-end atomicity for free: its check-then-update sequences
   over the replay and pending logs (`replay_log`, `pending_log` at
   lib.rs:134-138) never interleave. Under axum, requests are concurrent.
   Preserve the CURRENT semantics: **wrap the replay log AND the pending log
   together in ONE `Mutex<SignState>`** (a small struct holding both), held
   across the WHOLE `handle_sign` call. **This narrow restructuring IS
   authorized and required** (codex audit 2026-07-16): `Node`'s two `RefCell`s
   make it non-`Sync`, so axum cannot share it as state without this change —
   "do not restructure Node" (below) means do not reorganize its OTHER fields
   or split policy state, NOT "leave the two logs as un-shareable RefCells."
   **Two separate log mutexes remain FORBIDDEN** (interleaved check/update
   between two concurrent identical requests would corrupt replay semantics —
   the two logs must move under one lock). `/events` state, the alert queue,
   and watchtower state stay independently accessible (their own
   `Arc<Mutex<..>>` as today), so `/events` never waits behind `/sign`.
   Document at the lock: **`/sign` is serialized BY DESIGN** — concurrency buys
   ISOLATION of `/sign` from `/events`/`/channel`, NOT sign-vs-sign throughput;
   two `/sign` requests still run one-at-a-time and that is correct. Run the (synchronous,
   CPU-bearing) `handle_sign` body inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` so
   descriptor scans/secp work never stall the runtime. **An accepted sign job
   must NOT be cancelled by a handler timeout** — a half-run sign that mutated
   the replay/pending log then got dropped is a ghost side effect; let accepted
   `/sign` work run to completion (the handler timeout guards connection
   liveness, not the committed sign job). Concretely: wrap the `spawn_blocking`
   JoinHandle in `tokio::time::timeout`; on timeout, drop the response future
   (the client gets a timeout status) but let the blocking task finish and
   commit its verdict. Recovery is by idempotent resubmission — the anti-replay
   log returns the recorded verdict for an identical commitment (DESIGN.md
   "anti-replay log" §, job (1) idempotency).
4. **Delete `http.rs`** — do not keep two HTTP stacks. Its `parse_since` unit
   test moves/adapts to wherever cursor parsing now lives.
5. **`main.rs`** becomes `#[tokio::main]`; serve the one axum app on
   `listen_port`.
6. **Watchtower driver**: `Node::spawn_watchtower`'s interval thread becomes a
   tokio interval task whose tick body runs via `spawn_blocking` (the tick
   calls blocking bitcoind JSON-RPC in `chain.rs`; a slow RPC must never stall
   the async runtime). `chain.rs` itself does NOT need an async rewrite.
7. **`Node` stays as it is** otherwise — apart from the authorized
   `Mutex<SignState>` change in step 3, do not reorganize its other fields,
   split policy state, or make policy code async.

## Tests (`vault-node`)
- All existing unit tests pass unchanged (policy, handle_sign, watchtower,
  replay) — except `http.rs`'s `parse_since` test, which moves with the code.
- **HTTP-level regression tests (NEW — the point of this task):** over a real
  loopback socket against the axum app:
  - `POST /sign` valid body → 200, exact response JSON shape.
  - `POST /sign` garbage → 400 `{"error": ...}`.
  - Oversized body (> 1 MiB) → rejected with the axum-standard status —
    assert the status you get and lock it as the contract; never 500 or hang.
  - `GET /events?since=42` and bare `/events` → cursor semantics unchanged.
  - Unknown route → 404; wrong method → assert-and-lock the axum answer.
- **Concurrency regression:** two identical `/sign` requests submitted
  concurrently → exactly one fresh acceptance path runs; replay/pending logs
  end consistent (no interleaving corruption). (`/sign` serializes against
  `/sign` by design — do NOT assert two signs overlap.)
- **Isolation (test each cause SEPARATELY, not as an "or" — codex audit):**
  (i) a slow/blocking `/sign` in flight → `GET /events` still responds
  promptly; (ii) a watchtower tick against a slow chain backend → `/events`
  still responds promptly; (iii) a **stalled client holding incomplete request
  headers open** → a separate `/events` request succeeds promptly (proves the
  per-connection-task model removed head-of-line blocking). This is what the
  async migration buys; it is NOT sign-vs-sign parallelism. (`/channel` gets
  the same isolation guarantee in V0-8a, where it exists.)
- **No-cancel sign job:** a `/sign` that exceeds the handler timeout returns a
  timeout status to the client, BUT the accepted job completes and commits its
  verdict (replay/pending logs consistent), and an identical resubmission
  returns the recorded verdict — no ghost half-run, no lost sign. (Assert all
  three: client sees timeout, log mutated once, resubmit is idempotent.)
- `nix develop -c cargo run -p vault-cli -- demo first-light` exits 0.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/`, the workspace `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock`
  only. Do NOT add any channel/peer code (V0-8a), do NOT touch the
  coordinator, policy-core, vault-proto, or the demo. Do NOT change any
  request/response JSON schema.
- Target ≤ 700 lines net including the new tests. If materially more, stop
  and simplify.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check`, `nix develop -c cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `nix develop -c cargo test --workspace` pass.
- `http.rs` no longer exists; the node serves `/sign` + `/events` via axum
  meeting the compatibility contract, proven by the HTTP-level regression
  tests, including the sign-path atomicity test.
- `demo first-light` exits 0.


---
## Polish notes (bead-polish-loop 2026-07-16)
- **This bead unblocks btc-policy-byf (the node channel) and MUST merge first.** It is a behavior-neutral migration — reviewers should confirm no observable /sign or /events behavior changed except the deliberately-locked axum edge statuses (413/405/404 bodies).
- **Authoritative design source (committed):** the "fully async, one port" decision is docs/DESIGN.md + the 2026-07-16 eng review; tmpfs reboot-death is docs/adr/0007-node-death-on-reboot.md. No ADR schema changes in this task.

title: Latched-repair state pays a full scantxoutset every 10s pass (hn8 follow-up)
description: Fable hn8 review [P3], independent finding. Compound-failure state: a reorg below the wallet's completion anchor sets the repair latch AND the re-import keeps failing (read-only wallet dir, wallet support removed mid-flight). Each 10s SCAN_INTERVAL pass then takes the cold branch, because 'repair_pending && !repair_in_progress' refuses the delta base (crates/vault-node/src/chain.rs ~1506-1513), so EVERY pass pays a full scantxoutset (~10.4s on signet, serialized process-wide across every node sharing the bitcoind) purely to re-derive a birthday for a repair that keeps failing. Pre-hn8 this corner delta-advanced after a single scan, so it is a regression in that specific state. AVAILABILITY ONLY — verdicts stay correct, the cache stays complete — but it degrades exactly the property this bead was for, under a failure the operator may not notice (see the sibling /healthz surfacing bead). FIX SHAPE: let a still-anchored scan-derived cache serve as the delta base while latched, re-scanning only once per repair ATTEMPT rather than once per pass — the latch protects the WALLET, not the cache, and an active-anchored cold cache is safe to delta-advance. Gates: fmt/clippy-D/workspace tests incl. the scripted-RPC chain suite, attack 16/16, all 3 demos.

title: V0-4b (core): two-track duress state machine
description:
## V0-4b (CORE): two-track duress state machine. Folded audit r2 (armed combine window is T-based not commitment-expiry-capped — resolves the empty-window sweep failure). Depends on V0-8b + V0-4a + V0-10.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file gitignored):

# V0-4b (core): two-track duress state machine

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Prerequisites merged:** V0-8b (node combine+broadcast with **release-at-fire**
  partial gate, **paired spend+escape candidates** registered + signed at ingress,
  the **coordinator-authenticated `request` channel carrier** that propagates a
  request to all peers, the ChainBackend package-acceptance + authorized-set),
  V0-4a (dual-pin both-Argon2 constant-time compare, per-node attempt budget with
  the arm-even-when-locked-out hook, Lockdown + FRAUD_SUSPECTED), **V0-10**
  (recovery-path branch + recovery spend — so "funds frozen → recovery" is a
  demonstrable exit).
- **AUTHORITATIVE, READ IN FULL: `docs/adr/0012-...` "Duress state machine (per
  node) — normative"** (two-track model, transition table, 8 invariants, V0-4
  implementation-semantics checklist) + the escape-admissibility paragraphs
  ("Nodes validate the escape…", "Build over the mempool UTXO set…",
  "Class-aware escape coverage…"). Also ADR-0013 §3 (class), §6 (coverage,
  feerate, epsilon, duress_delay_secs, refresh bounds), `CONTEXT.md`.
- The **adversarial regtest/CLI harness is a SEPARATE dependent bead**
  (V0-4b-harness); this bead is the production state machine + its unit/model
  tests only.

## Outcome
A valid, coordinator-authenticated **duress-pin** request **unconditionally**
freezes hot-class finalization and schedules **Lockdown at T** (the SAFETY track,
keyed on the pin ALONE — chain-view-independent), while a **best-effort Firing
sweep** of the user-signed escape is attempted at T (the SWEEP track, gated by
the full admissibility predicate at FIRE-TIME only). Sweep failure = funds frozen
→ recovery (V0-10), never theft. Silent to an outside attacker.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node`)

### 1. Which transition rows this bead owns
V0-8b already implements the NORMAL rows (`Idle + normal SpendRequest`,
`Idle + RefreshRequest`, `Scheduled + fire-time`) via sign-at-ingress +
release-at-fire. This bead adds the DURESS rows of the ADR-0012 table and MUST
NOT weaken the normal rows or invariant 7 (release-at-fire). Implement verbatim:
`Idle + duress` → Armed; `Scheduled + valid duress (coord OR peer)` → suppress
the scheduled spend then Arm; `Armed + peer duress` → arm idempotently;
`Armed/Scheduled + hot spend while Armed` → refuse finalize, `T ← min(T, its
Hold-expiry − ε)`; `Armed + clock reaches T` → **Lockdown UNCONDITIONALLY** +
spawn Firing job; `Firing` (orthogonal); `Lockdown + request` → FRAUD_SUSPECTED;
`Lockdown + peer sweep-combine` → accepted; `Armed + reboot` → node death.

### 2. Initial T computation (codex D4 — SECURITY, was omitted)
`T = min(first_seen_duress + duress_delay_secs, earliest_pending_hot_fire − ε)`.
- Recompute (shrink only) when a new hot spend is accepted while Armed.
- **Bounded ε** validation (a small margin; reject absurd ε).
- **Past/matured case:** if the computed T is already past (or a pending hot
  spend's public Hold-expiry precedes T), **fire immediately**. Rationale: a
  previously-pending hot spend must NOT settle at its publicly-expected
  Hold-expiry AFTER a later T — that visible non-settlement during the hostage
  window would reveal duress. State the formula, recomputation rule, ε bound,
  and past-means-fire-now semantics explicitly.

### 3. Constant-observable ingress — fully closed (codex D7, silence)
Every request (normal OR duress) does the identical observable work; the pin
(V0-4a compare) flips only an internal fire bit. Explicitly:
- **Both pins propagate the same coordinator-signed request** to peers (V0-8b's
  `request` carrier) — identical peer-fanout **count, order, payload size, and
  retry policy**.
- **Neither candidate's partial is transmitted until its fire** (invariant 7 —
  spend AND escape).
- Identical **HTTP status / body / length / release deadline** for a valid normal
  vs a valid duress request; **peer failures cannot alter the pin-dependent
  response path** (the response does not wait on, or vary with, peer-fanout
  outcomes).
- The same-shaped **two-slot schedule record** (immediate + delayed slot) is
  written to RAMDISK on both pins (escape-class delayed slot is a no-op under
  normal; a residual sweep under duress). One atomic RAMDISK write; never durable
  disk (a durable "duress detected" record is forbidden, ADR-0008).
- **Response cover:** `pending`/`first_seen`/remaining-Hold reported identically
  under both pins; never expose Armed-vs-Scheduled or the real fire-time before T.

### 4. The 8 invariants (ADR-0012) — implement, do NOT weaken
(i) Lockdown at T unconditional (never waits for escape confirmation — EVERY
fire-failure branch still Locks Down at T); (ii) arming/lockdown
chain-view-independent (pin alone); (iii) reboot-death (RAMDISK, nothing
persists); (iv) pin-compare constant-cost (V0-4a); (v) fail-closed lockout (valid
duress arms regardless of lockout, via V0-4a's hook); (vi) idempotency before
cache (process the pin/safety signal BEFORE any cached commitment verdict, so a
duress resubmission with a fresh nonce of a previously-normal-pending commitment
still arms); (vii) partial-release authorization (arming atomically + monotonically
suppresses every existing/future hot-partial release — installed timers + cached
commitments — for BOTH candidates); (viii) escape-class two-slot record.

### 5. Full escape-admissibility predicate (codex D6 — FIRE-TIME only, never arm gates)
At the Firing job (T), the sweep fires only if armed-set has **t distinct valid
escape signers per input** AND the escape is admissible. The FULL predicate
(ADR-0012 — not just three labels):
- **coverage** ≥ threshold (e.g. 95%), **class-aware** (ADR-0012 "Class-aware
  escape coverage"): hot-class spend frozen → escape supersedes it, coverage over
  confirmed + vault-authorized-unconfirmed; escape-class spend completes → escape
  inputs **disjoint** from the completed spend, coverage over their **union**;
- **feerate** ≥ panic floor;
- **final `nLockTime`** + **non-relative-locking `nSequence`** (`0xffffffff` —
  also makes E non-RBF-signaling so the fixed-panic-fee rebroadcast loop is sound);
- **every input confirmed OR a vault-authorized-unconfirmed parent** (own
  spend-change/refresh — never an external unconfirmed deposit; toxic-deposit
  safe);
- **full package `testmempoolaccept`** (E + its unconfirmed vault-authorized
  ancestors), not merely relay-standard.
Each admissibility FAILURE → the sweep does not fire; **Lockdown at T still
happens unconditionally** → funds frozen → recovery. NEVER an arm gate.

### 6. Refresh rules under duress (codex D5)
- **Any pending spend blocks all refreshes** (already V0-8b subordination) — do
  not let a disjoint refresh invalidate escape inputs during `[arm, T]`.
- The **escape-class exception** per ADR-0012 (escape-class completes; residual
  sweep over the union).
- **No pin-dependent cancellation:** there is NO operation whose presence/timing
  depends on the pin that could become a duress oracle. Any cancel/supersede is
  identical under both pins.

### 7. Candidate-registry duress obligations (deferred from V0-8a D13)
- **Armed-candidate expiry exemption + fire-complete cleanup:** an armed/
  scheduled-to-fire candidate is EXEMPT from the commitment-expiry sweep AND the
  `/channel`-lookup expiry rejection until its fire completes (escape-class T =
  `first_seen + duress_delay_secs` can exceed `max_commitment_age_secs`); finite
  lifecycle (cleared on fire-complete) so it cannot pin the capacity cap.
- **Armed combine window is T-based, NOT commitment-expiry-capped (codex fix
  2026-07-17 — resolves the empty-window contradiction):** V0-8b caps a NORMAL
  candidate's combine window at `min(commitment_expiry, fire_time +
  combine_slack_secs)`. But a duress escape's `T` can land AFTER
  `commitment_expiry`, which would make that window EMPTY — no partial could be
  released or collected and every such sweep would deterministically fail. For an
  **armed/escape candidate the combine window is `[T, T + combine_slack_secs]`**
  (the commitment-expiry cap does NOT apply — the candidate is already exempt
  from expiry pruning, so its combine window must be too). Partials for the armed
  escape are released at T and collected within this T-based window. State this
  as the reconciliation of the armed-expiry-exemption with V0-8b's normal-window
  cap.
- **Capacity gate AFTER pin/safety:** the candidate-store capacity check runs
  AFTER arm/freeze so a duress request is never dropped for fullness.
- **Firing job bound (codex nit):** define when the never-confirming
  rebroadcast job ends / how it stays resource-bounded while the node is locked
  down (e.g. bounded retries / until commitment-relevant horizon).

## Tests (unit/model — the V0-4 checklist; broad regtest lives in V0-4b-harness)
- **Atomic monotonic Armed overlay** (barrier-controlled REPEATED races, not one
  scheduler-dependent race): pending hot spend + duress arm racing its
  Hold-expiry → the pre-pending partial never slips out.
- **Both-Argon2 + constant-time-select** (structural, from V0-4a): normal/duress/
  wrong indistinguishable in Argon2 count + budget touch.
- **Fail-closed lockout**: lock out C/D/E on wrong pins, then the real duress
  request still arms.
- **Idempotency ordering**: normal-pending commitment resubmitted with the duress
  pin + fresh nonce → arms.
- **Partial-release**: no partial (spend OR escape) leaves before its fire; a
  compromised peer soliciting at ingress gets none.
- **Response cover**: direct response byte/status/length comparison + `/events`
  comparison under both pins → identical until T; peer-message trace + fanout
  count/order/size identical; timer/lock/write instrumentation identical.
- **Initial T**: pre-pending, matured-pending (fire-now), and a nearer post-arm
  hot spend (shrink T).
- **Unconditional Lockdown**: assert Lockdown at T for sweep-success, `< t`,
  coverage-fail, feerate-fail, package-fail, broadcast-fail, and
  never-confirming broadcast — every branch.
- **Lockdown behavior**: accepts in-flight sweep-combine partials while rejecting
  ALL new signing (FRAUD_SUSPECTED).
- **Candidate exemption**: armed candidate exempt at BOTH prune paths (sweep +
  `/channel` lookup); cleaned up after fire; capacity released.
- **Escape-class**: normal delayed-slot no-op vs duress residual sweep (disjoint
  inputs, union coverage).
- **Reboot-death**: DEPLOYMENT death (delete the simulated tmpfs deployment) —
  arm t+1, kill one before T → sweep still fires; drop below t → lockdown-only
  (no sweep, no theft); the killed node cannot restart/rejoin.
- **Arm-split closed**: no unarmed sub-quorum can complete a coerced hot spend
  after any node received the valid duress request (via request propagation).

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/` only. CONSUME V0-8b (channel, carrier, candidates,
  broadcast), V0-4a (pin, budget, Lockdown), V0-10 (recovery). Do NOT rework the
  channel wire, the combine/broadcast plumbing, or the pin substrate. Do NOT
  build the broad adversarial regtest/CLI harness (that is V0-4b-harness). Do NOT
  add device-bound duress tokens, dynamic policy, or duress_response toggles
  (rejected). RAMDISK only — no durable duress signal.
- Build the two-track machine EXACTLY per ADR-0012; do not invent behavior the
  ADR doesn't specify or weaken any invariant to satisfy a reviewer. Size
  advisory; never compress invariants, transition rows, or checklist tests.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- Every duress transition row + all 8 invariants + the full fire-time
  admissibility predicate + initial-T semantics + constant-observable-ingress
  closure implemented; the V0-4 implementation-semantics checklist unit/model
  tests pass. The two-track machine is live; the broad adversarial demonstration
  is V0-4b-harness.
