description: Fable hn8 review [P3], re-check item 5 — STILL OPEN after 6 rb-lite rounds, downgraded from P2. A bitcoind without usable wallet RPC (-disablewallet, unwritable wallet dir, wallet support absent) silently pins the node to the scantxoutset fallback FOREVER. The fallback is complete, correct, and verdict-identical — so this is not a safety issue — but it silently forfeits the entire readiness/latency win btc-policy-hn8 exists for (measured: ~10.4s per scan on signet's 72.2M-output set, serialized process-wide across all five nodes), and the only signal today is two eprintln lines in the node's own log. FIX: a pin-independent boolean on /healthz (e.g. vault_wallet_serving) fed from existing state; full_scan_count() already exists as the natural hook. SILENCE-SAFE: the refresher never reads pin/duress/arm state, so the field cannot vary by pin class — but the /healthz field set is a SILENCE surface, so the byte-identity tests (healthz_is_byte_identical_on_an_armed_pre_t_node) must be extended to cover it, and the field must be identical on armed and idle twins. Consider also a startup capability probe in verify_required_indexes (chain.rs ~666) so a misconfigured backend is loud at boot rather than silently slow forever.

title: Hardware-signing path for the user key (PSBT hand-off)
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (Fable #2). docs/DESIGN.md premise 1 is 'a user hardware key AND a t-of-n quorum', and threat rows A2/A3 turn on the user key being stealable-but-not-sufficient. In code the user key is SOFTWARE in every driver (Actor::random / in-process secp keys), and there is no cyberkrill, HWI, or PSBT hand-off anywhere in the tree.

WHY IT IS P1: on a real deployment the software user key would live on the coordinator host — the one machine ADR-0012 already names as the SEVERE residual (a pre-wrench coordinator compromise reads the normal PIN and substitutes it, silently nullifying duress). A software user key on that same host MERGES adversary A3 with that residual: the attacker skips the wrench entirely for the hot-bounded portion. The design's core premise is currently false in code.

DELIVER: a PSBT hand-off seam — the coordinator composes the spend and its mandatory escape, exports PSBTs, a hardware device DISPLAYS and signs them, and the signed PSBTs come back. Reuse the user's own tooling where it fits (cyberkrill / HWI) rather than adding a dependency; see the standing rule in docs/SBOM-AND-DEPENDENCY-POLICY.md.

CARE — the display is the security boundary: the device must show the user what they are actually authorizing (destination, amount, and that a mandatory escape is co-signed), or the hand-off adds ceremony without adding safety. A device that blind-signs a PSBT the coordinator composed defends nothing against a compromised coordinator, which is the entire point.

NON-GOALS: choosing a specific vendor; multisig-on-device UX; changing the descriptor.

VERIFY: an honest spend completes with the user key never present in the coordinator process; a test or documented drill showing what the device displays for a spend AND for its escape.

title: V0-8a: node-to-node channel (signed envelopes + verified partial exchange)
description:
## Outcome
vault-node gains an authenticated node-to-node channel: per-message signed envelopes (no session) over POST /channel on the existing axum app, plus a verified partial-signature exchange primitive backed by a candidate registry populated by the real /sign path. These are the primitives V0-8b drives to combine + broadcast; this task builds ONLY the channel layer.

## Why this exists
Under Model B the coordinator is a pure relay: nodes assemble the t-of-n signature among themselves and broadcast. That requires an authenticated channel that carries signatures and assembly only — never policy — and a way for a node to verify a peer's partial against its OWN recomputed sighash (never blind-merge a peer PSBT). ADR-0012 "The node-to-node channel" + ADR-0013 §4 (manifest) are authoritative.

## Critical security properties (must all hold)
- Channel identity endorsed by the node's Bitcoin signing key, verified against the immutable manifest — the coordinator cannot mint/impersonate a node.
- Per-message possession proof (envelope signature over a fresh nonce+timestamp) — no session handshake.
- recipient_node_id binds each envelope to its receiver — closes cross-recipient replay for THIS and every future msg_type.
- Signature covers the RAW payload_b64 field (verify BEFORE decode) — identity before payload parsing.
- Partials verified against the expected descriptor pubkey over the node's OWN registered sighash — never blind-merge.
- Signing-oracle prohibition: structurally no channel message can cause the node to sign.

## Non-goals / scope guard
Touch crates/vault-node/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock ONLY. The ONLY /sign-path change is the register_candidate post-verdict funnel. Do NOT build combine/broadcast (V0-8b), duress state machine (V0-4), Tor/mTLS (v1), full manifest provisioning (V0-9), or any session/connection state. Target ~1200-1600 lines incl tests.

## Verification (ship gate)
fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace green; demo first-light exits 0; the two-in-process-nodes E2E exchanges one verified partial THROUGH the real /sign→/channel path (no test-only candidate injection).

## Deployment context (ADR-0007)
tmpfs/ramdisk: reboot = bare machine = permanent node death; a dead node never rejoins the immutable manifest (restore capacity = rotate to a successor vault). No channel state persists.

---
FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained executable memory; the rb-lite task file this was transferred from is gitignored):

# V0-8a: node-to-node channel — identity, signed envelopes, partial-signature exchange

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run EVERY cargo/bitcoind command through the flake dev
  shell: `nix develop -c cargo test`, etc. Plain `cargo` fails.
- **Prerequisite: V0-8a0 (axum migration) is merged.** The node is async
  (tokio + axum, one port, `http.rs` deleted, sign-path Mutex +
  spawn_blocking). Build the channel as routes and tasks on that base. All new
  code is async.
- Read `docs/adr/0012-model-b-spend-and-duress-architecture.md` (**"The
  node-to-node channel"** section — the authoritative security properties) and
  `docs/adr/0013-concrete-protocol-schemas.md` (§4 manifest — the
  channel-identity root). Also `CONTEXT.md` ("Node channel", "Manifest").
- This is the **channel layer only**. It does NOT rework the spend path or the
  coordinator (that is V0-8b). It provides the primitives V0-8b will drive:
  authenticated peer messaging + a verified partial-signature exchange.

## Problem description
Under Model B, nodes assemble the t-of-n signature among themselves and
broadcast (the coordinator is a pure relay). This task builds the
**authenticated peer messaging** those nodes use, and the **partial-signature
exchange** primitive — but NOT the combine/broadcast wiring or the spend-path
rework (V0-8b). The channel carries signatures and assembly only, **never
policy**.

Design decisions locked by the 2026-07-16 eng review (do not re-litigate):
- **No session handshake.** Every peer message is a self-authenticating
  **signed envelope** (possession is proven per message — the fresh
  nonce+timestamp IS the challenge). This satisfies ADR-0012's
  challenge-response/possession requirement with no connection state machine.
- **Same port.** Channel messages are a route (`POST /channel`) on the node's
  one axum app. Axum's concurrency removes the head-of-line-blocking that
  motivated a separate port; layered DoS guards handle peer spam.
  **Principle (2026-07-16): no endpoint on a node derives ANY authority from
  network reachability — all authority is cryptographic, rooted in the
  manifest.** The coordinator can reach `/channel` and peers can reach
  `/sign`; both gain nothing (envelopes need an endorsed channel key; sign
  requests need user/coordinator signatures). Firewalls are hygiene, never a
  trust boundary.
- **Node-local types.** The envelope types live in `vault-node` — the
  coordinator never parses channel messages (V0-8b is also node-side).
- **Reboot survival is a NON-goal.** The whole node runs from **tmpfs/ramdisk**
  (ADR-0007): reboot = bare machine = **permanent node death** (a dead node
  never rejoins the immutable manifest; restoring capacity means rotating to a
  successor vault, not resurrecting the node). No channel state (nonce cache,
  partial store, candidates) needs to persist.
  Derivation determinism (below) exists so the setup-time endorsement matches
  the runtime key — not to survive reboots.
- **Outbound HTTP client = `reqwest`** (user decision 2026-07-16): V0-8b/V0-4
  and v1 (SOCKS/Tor) reuse it.

## Required changes (`crates/vault-node` + workspace manifests)

### 1. Channel identity (ADR-0012)
Each node has a **RAM-only channel keypair**, derived **deterministically**
from the node's key material:
`channel_seckey = tagged_hash("btc-policy/channel-key/v0", node_seckey)`
interpreted as a big-endian scalar. **Retry algorithm (codex audit — make it
deterministic):** if the 32-byte digest is zero or ≥ the secp256k1 curve order,
re-hash `tagged_hash("btc-policy/channel-key/v0", node_seckey || counter)` with
a u8 `counter` starting at 0 and incrementing until the result is a valid
scalar (probability of even one retry is ~2^-128; the loop is for total
determinism, not practical reach). Write the tag string once as a const. Never persisted; derived
at startup. Deterministic so the setup-time endorsement and the runtime key
always agree; must differ from the signing key. (V0-9 swaps the seed input to
wskdf without changing the shape.)

The channel pubkey is **endorsed by the node's Bitcoin signing key** over a
domain-separated structure `(wallet_id, manifest_hash, node_id,
channel_pubkey, protocol_version, transport_endpoints)`. A node accepts a
peer's channel identity **only** if the endorsement verifies against a signing
pubkey bound to that `node_id` in the (immutable) manifest for this vault.
The coordinator cannot mint or impersonate a node.

### 2. Manifest + config (minimal but real — full provisioning is V0-9)
**The `[channel]` config block is OPTIONAL (codex audit 2026-07-16 — resolves
the demo contradiction).** Absent ⇒ **absent-channel mode**: the `/channel`
route is NOT mounted, NO manifest/bijection/endorsement invariants run, and the
node behaves exactly as today. This is what lets `demo first-light` (which does
not use the channel) keep passing **without editing the demo** — the demo omits
`[channel]`. Present ⇒ every invariant below applies and `/channel` is mounted.
- The `[channel]` block carries: `node_id` (this node's id) and `nodes` — the
  FULL membership list of all `n` entries **including this node itself**, each
  `{ node_id, endpoints, signing_pubkey, channel_pubkey, channel_endorsement }`.
  (`nodes`, not `peers`, and self is included — the manifest hash needs all `n`;
  self-inclusion removes the "does peers contain me?" ambiguity.) **`endpoints`
  is PLURAL** — a `Vec` of endpoint strings (a node may advertise clearnet +
  onion), matching the endorsement/manifest `transport_endpoints` byte-for-byte
  (codex audit 2026-07-16: there is no singular `endpoint` anywhere; the config,
  the hashed manifest, and the endorsement domain all use the same plural list).
  **`channel_pubkey` is REQUIRED** on every entry. At startup assert the
  `node_id`s form an **exact `0..n-1` bijection** with the descriptor's
  canonical node keys (§1 ordering); a gap, dup, or out-of-range id is fatal.
- **Endpoint consistency (codex I4):** assert this node's own entry's
  `endpoints` includes the address the daemon actually binds `/channel` on, and
  that every node's `endpoints` are canonical and parseable — a manifest
  endorsing one self endpoint set while the daemon binds another silently drops
  the node from the combine set. Fatal config error on mismatch.
- **Resource-limit config (all in `[channel]`, units + CONCRETE defaults —
  ADR-0013 §5):** `max_active_candidates` (count, default **1024**),
  `max_candidate_store_bytes` (bytes, default **67_108_864 = 64 MiB**; byte
  accounting = stored PSBT + sighashes + partials per candidate),
  `per_peer_quota_per_min` (envelopes/min/peer, default **600**),
  `max_concurrent_channel_requests` (pre-auth global bound, default **64**),
  `max_msg_bytes` (default **1_048_576 = 1 MiB**), `max_response_bytes`
  (outbound read bound, default **65_536**), `per_send_deadline_secs` (default
  **5**). Every field has a default so a minimal `[channel]` block is valid.
- **Two-pass construction (no hash cycle):** the canonical manifest is the
  endorsement-FREE structure
  `(wallet_id, nodes[node_id, signing_pubkey, channel_pubkey,
  transport_endpoints] ordered by node_id, protocol_version)` —
  **`channel_pubkey` IS in the hashed structure** (deterministic, so known at
  setup before endorsements; the manifest exists to pin channel identity).
  `manifest_hash` = tagged SHA-256 over its canonical serialization;
  endorsements are computed OVER that hash and distributed alongside, never
  inside it (ADR-0013 §4). **This v0 `manifest_hash` is PROVISIONAL:** V0-9
  defines the final canonical serialization of the full §4 struct (adding
  vault_descriptor, coordinator_auth_pubkey, t/n, allowlist,
  escape_descriptor) and all endorsements re-derive then — no
  hash continuity is promised before the provisioning ceremony.
- **Startup invariants (assert, fail to start otherwise):** this node's own
  signing pubkey is one of the descriptor's node keys; every manifest signing
  pubkey is one of the descriptor's node keys; `node_id` ↔ descriptor-key
  mapping is total and unambiguous (this mapping is also what "expected
  descriptor pubkey for signer X" below means). **Additionally (codex audit
  2026-07-16):** the node's LOCALLY-derived channel pubkey must equal its own
  `nodes[self]` `channel_pubkey` entry (a valid-but-mismatched self entry
  otherwise makes the node permanently unreachable — its peers verify against a
  key it never signs with); and when a config carries an `expected_manifest_hash`,
  the computed provisional `manifest_hash` must equal it (ADR-0013 trust-root
  posture — the node is sealed to a specific manifest).

### 3. Signed envelopes = peer authentication (the wire contract — exact)

**Domain-separation tags (all tagged SHA-256; fixed consts, codex audit
2026-07-16 — every digest in the system MUST name its tag so independent
derivations agree):**
- channel-key derivation: `"btc-policy/channel-key/v0"`
- manifest hash: `"btc-policy/manifest/v0"` (over the §2 BaseManifest canonical
  bytes)
- channel-key endorsement: `"btc-policy/channel-endorsement/v0"` (over the
  §1 domain-separated structure)
- envelope signature preimage: `"btc-policy/channel-envelope/v0"`
- `user_sig_hash`: `"btc-policy/user-sig-hash/v0"`
**Byte conventions (fixed):** all pubkeys 33-byte compressed (raw in preimages,
hex only in JSON); all hashes 32-byte raw in preimages, lowercase hex in JSON;
`nonce` 16 random bytes (hex in JSON, raw in preimage). **Length-prefix rule
(codex audit 2026-07-16):** ONLY variable-length fields (`payload_b64` bytes,
`endpoints` strings, script bytes, DER sigs) get a u32-LE length prefix;
**fixed-width numeric fields (timestamp u64, node_id u16, input index u32,
protocol_version u32, version i32, lock_time u32, sequence u32) are written at
their fixed width LE with NO length prefix** (they are self-delimiting). Pick a
width per numeric field and keep it fixed.
**Encoding ownership (v0 — DESIGN "wire format greenfield until v1"):** the
implementer OWNS the exact canonical byte layout of every preimage (per-digest
field order, the fixed numeric widths above, endpoint serialization) and MUST
**document it in a single module-level table in code** so signer and verifier
provably read the same bytes. v0 is single-workspace, so cross-implementation
byte-stability is NOT required until v1; the requirement here is INTERNAL
consistency + regression-locking, not conformance to an external standard.
**Golden vectors (test requirement — strengthened, codex B3 fix 2026-07-16):**
freeze the chosen layout by hard-coding, per digest (channel-key derivation,
manifest hash, endorsement digest, envelope digest, user_sig_hash), BOTH the
**expected canonical preimage bytes** AND the resulting digest — not just the
digest. A vector that only pins the digest, generated from the same
canonicalizer under test, can bless a common-mode omission (e.g. signer AND
verifier both skip `nonce` → an attacker mutates the nonce and replays inside
the timestamp window while round-trip tests still pass). Pinning the preimage
bytes catches that. **Additionally: per-field mutation of the ENVELOPE** — flip
each signed field (`msg_type`, `protocol_version`, `wallet_id`, `manifest_hash`,
`sender_node_id`, `recipient_node_id`, `payload_b64`, **`nonce`, `timestamp`**)
one at a time and assert each mutation invalidates `channel_sig`. Round-trip
tests separately prove signer == verifier.

Every channel message is one JSON envelope:
`{ msg_type, protocol_version, wallet_id, manifest_hash, sender_node_id,
   recipient_node_id, payload_b64, nonce, timestamp, channel_sig }`
- **Crypto:** secp256k1 ECDSA; 33-byte compressed pubkeys; DER signatures
  (consistent with the node's existing signing stack).
- **Signature preimage:** tagged SHA-256 (`"btc-policy/channel-envelope/v0"`)
  over a **canonical length-prefixed byte serialization** of
  `(msg_type, protocol_version, wallet_id, manifest_hash, sender_node_id,
  recipient_node_id, payload_b64_bytes, nonce, timestamp)` — fixed field
  order, applying the **Byte conventions rule below as normative** (codex fix
  2026-07-16, resolving the earlier contradiction): variable-length fields
  (`msg_type`, `payload_b64_bytes`, `nonce`) get a u32-LE length prefix;
  fixed-width numerics (`protocol_version` u32, `sender_node_id`/
  `recipient_node_id` u16, `timestamp` u64) are written at their declared width
  LE with NO prefix; `wallet_id`/`manifest_hash` are fixed 32 raw bytes, no
  prefix. There is NO "u64 for all numeric fields" rule — that wording is
  retracted. One shared canonicalizer produces this; the module table + golden
  vectors record the exact per-field widths. **Sign the
  raw ASCII bytes of the `payload_b64` field, NOT the decoded payload**
  (codex-review fix 2026-07-16: decoding before signature verification is
  forbidden — "identity before payload parsing" — so the signature must cover
  the un-decoded base64 field; the node verifies the envelope, THEN
  base64-decodes `payload_b64`). NOT over serialized JSON.
- **`protocol_version`** is in the envelope AND the preimage; a node rejects
  any envelope whose `protocol_version` ≠ the manifest-pinned version (the
  version lives on the envelope, not the payload; ADR-0013 §4's `BaseManifest`
  pins it). **v0 constant: `protocol_version = 0`** — the minimal in-memory
  manifest sets it to `0` and the node compares against that; define it as a
  named const (`PROTOCOL_VERSION_V0 = 0`), not a magic literal. (V0-9's real
  provisioning carries the same field forward.)
- **`recipient_node_id`** binds the envelope to its intended receiver: a node
  rejects any envelope whose `recipient_node_id` ≠ its own `node_id`. Closes
  cross-recipient replay for THIS and every future `msg_type` (a directed
  message a peer replays to a different node fails the bind), so replay-safety
  never rests on idempotency alone.
- **`payload_b64` is opaque:** base64 of canonical payload bytes, decoded only
  AFTER the envelope authenticates.
- `timestamp`: u64 unix seconds; `nonce`: 16 random bytes, hex.
- **Freshness window (decided 2026-07-16):** accept
  `timestamp ∈ [now − 300s, now + 60s]` — 5 min past tolerance (v1 Tor
  latency + retries + skew), 60s future (skew only). Two `const`s with the
  rationale in a comment, NOT config (hygiene knob, not a ceremony knob — the
  window is hygiene, not safety: every planned msg_type is recipient-bound +
  idempotent). **Nonce-cache prune keys on the envelope's `timestamp`, not
  receipt time** (Fable-review fix 2026-07-16): retain a nonce until
  `timestamp < now − 300` — pruning a future-stamped envelope by receipt time
  would reopen a ~60s replay window. Nodes never exchange or negotiate time —
  no inter-node time protocol, ever (attacker-influenceable input to a hygiene
  mechanism); hosts run NTP (v1 deployment guidance). Use a **monotonic
  high-water mark** for `now` in both the freshness test and the nonce prune
  (never let `now` go backwards) — a backwards NTP step would otherwise let
  pruned nonces re-enter the window with an empty cache. **Count freshness
  rejections per peer and surface them through the existing alert queue /
  `GET /events` path** (codex I2 — a concrete operator-visible surface, not a
  bare counter): emit a structured event carrying the peer `node_id`, the
  running reject count, and a clock-skew hint, so an operator sees WHICH node's
  clock is off before it is silently ejected from the combine set.
  **PRESERVE the existing watchtower event JSON** (codex audit 2026-07-16): the
  current alert shape (`watchtower.rs`) and its dedupe key assume every event
  has a txid/outpoint. Do NOT fabricate transaction fields for a freshness
  event — generalize the internal event to an enum (or give the freshness event
  an explicit dedupe key) so existing recovery-path/un-cosigned alerts keep
  their exact JSON and dedupe behavior. Test peer attribution, monotonic count,
  and visibility through `/events`, AND that existing watchtower alert JSON is
  unchanged. Also assert a
  saturated `/channel` verification load does NOT starve `/events` or the
  watchtower tick (the isolation the async migration bought).
- **Receiver verification order:** `protocol_version` = manifest's →
  **`wallet_id` = my vault's AND `manifest_hash` = mine** (explicit
  local-vault equality — codex fix 2026-07-16: the endorsement domain
  separator catches cross-vault indirectly, but a direct equality check is
  cleaner and independently testable) → `recipient_node_id` = my `node_id` →
  sender_node_id in manifest → endorsement valid → `channel_sig` valid over the
  recomputed preimage → `timestamp` within the freshness window → **atomically
  consume `(sender_node_id, nonce)`** (check-unseen-and-insert in ONE step,
  AFTER sig + freshness pass but BEFORE dispatch — codex B1 fix 2026-07-16:
  deferring nonce consumption until after acceptance would let an
  authenticated-but-rejected message be replayed; the seen-nonce set is keyed
  by authenticated `sender_node_id`) → only then base64-decode `payload_b64`
  and dispatch on `msg_type`.
- `msg_type` exists so V0-8b (combine coordination) and V0-4 (duress
  propagation) add message types without a wire break; this task implements
  exactly one: `partial`. **Every registered `msg_type` MUST be recipient-bound
  (via `recipient_node_id`) AND idempotent — each `msg_type` must define an
  explicit idempotency key and pass a duplicate-delivery test before it is
  registered for dispatch** (both-model fix 2026-07-16: "assert idempotent"
  can't enforce semantics, so make it a concrete gate — a type without a
  declared idempotency key + passing dup-delivery test does not ship). For
  `partial` the idempotency key is `(commitment_id, input, signer)` and
  re-delivery re-stores the already-verified partial (a no-op); the nonce
  check is hygiene on top.

### 4. Candidate registry (the seam that makes verification possible)
`/channel` must verify partials against this node's OWN canonical view — which
today dies as a local variable inside `handle_sign`. Add a
`register_candidate(...)` call on `handle_sign`'s **verdict paths** (both the
early-return `Pending` and the signed-response path). **A small, behavior-
preserving control-flow refactor of `handle_sign` is permitted** for this —
"exactly one call site" is not required and cannot cover both a Pending
early-return and a signed return while excluding refusals; a single
post-verdict funnel (`register on Pending|Signed, never on Refusal`) is the
clean shape (codex fix 2026-07-16). This is the ONLY spend-path CHANGE
permitted; do not alter any policy check, response shape, or the sign decision.
- **Keyed by `commitment_id`** (NOT bare unsigned-txid — codex/Fable fix
  2026-07-16: the same txid can have several live commitments with different
  expiry/user-signature instances; keying by txid would collide them). The
  record stores: `commitment_id`, the unsigned-txid (verified transaction
  identity — partials still bind to it), the canonical PSBT, per-input
  sighashes (recomputed by THIS node), the expected descriptor pubkey per
  (input, node_id), the spend's user-signature material, `user_sig_hash`
  (**tagged SHA-256 over the user's DER signature(s) + sighash-type byte(s),
  in input order, as this node verified them at ingress**), and the
  commitment expiry (its own, fixed eviction horizon — no extension).
  Registration reserves a candidate slot **after** the verdict. **In V0-8a, at
  capacity the candidate is simply NOT inserted** (log it; the `/sign` verdict
  and response are unchanged — there is no wire-level `AT_CAPACITY` refusal and
  no duress surface in this task). The full "capacity gate runs AFTER pin/safety
  so a duress arm/freeze is never suppressed" ordering is a **V0-4 obligation**
  (§ scope guard), because only V0-4 introduces the safety track that ordering
  protects.
Storage: `Arc<Mutex<PartialStore>>` on `Node` (the V0-8b Hold-expiry
timer task will read it too).
**Which verdicts register (decided 2026-07-16):** every NON-REFUSED verdict —
instantly-signed spends AND accepted-but-Pending hot spends, both at ingress
(V0-8b's Hold-expiry combine and Model B's sign-at-ingress require Pending
registration; a fast peer's partial arriving during our Hold then verifies
instead of bouncing as unknown-candidate). **Refused requests never
register** — nothing will ever combine for them, and refused junk must not
occupy the store. Escape candidates arrive with the tagged-request migration
(ADR-0013 §2) — out of V0-8a scope.

### 5. Partial-signature exchange (the core primitive)
The `partial` payload carries: `commitment_id`, `wallet_id`, the exact
unsigned-txid, input index, signer node id, sighash type, spend purpose,
`user_sig_hash`, and the partial signature (DER). (`protocol_version` is on the
envelope, not the payload.)
On receipt, after envelope authentication:
- **Equality checks:** payload `wallet_id` matches the envelope's;
  **`signer_node_id == sender_node_id`** (nodes only relay their own partials
  in V0-8a); the payload's txid matches the candidate's stored txid;
  `user_sig_hash` matches the registered candidate's.
- **Candidate check:** the `commitment_id` must be a **registered candidate**;
  a partial for an unknown commitment is answered `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`
  (retriable). The sender applies **bounded retry with backoff until the
  commitment expiry** — codex fix 2026-07-16: "re-sends at fire time" alone
  fails the escape-class immediate-fire case and races the concurrent fan-out,
  so an explicit bounded-retry rule (or a candidate-ready ack) is required, not
  an assumption. Do NOT hold unknown partials on the receiver.
- **`spend_purpose` is informational only** — nothing acts on it; transaction
  class is always derived locally (ADR-0012's node-derived class predicate).
- **Verify the partial** against the expected descriptor pubkey for
  (input, signer node id) over this node's **own registered sighash** before
  storing; import only verified signature fields into the canonical PSBT
  (**never blind-merge a peer PSBT**).
- **Structural store bound:** at most one partial per
  (candidate, input, signer); partials accepted only for registered
  candidates. No generic FIFO/LRU eviction — a compromised peer must not be
  able to evict quorum-useful partials.
- **Hard capacity cap (decided 2026-07-16, D12):** a configured maximum on
  active candidates AND total bytes, bounding RAM. **In V0-8a this gates ONLY
  the registry insertion, never the wire.** At capacity: the candidate is not
  inserted (log it), no live candidate is ever evicted (a compromised peer must
  not evict quorum-useful partials), and the `/sign` verdict/response is
  **unchanged** — there is no wire-level `AT_CAPACITY` message and no duress
  surface in this task. The insertion runs after the verdict, so the sign
  decision is never affected by store fullness.
  **V0-4 obligation (not built here):** once the duress safety track exists, the
  capacity check must run AFTER pin/safety so a duress SpendRequest still
  arms/freezes when the store is full (freeze + lockdown need no candidate slot;
  only the best-effort sweep candidate does) — preserving ADR-0012's "arming is
  keyed on the duress pin alone, unconditional, resource-independent." Recorded
  in the scope guard.
- **Eviction (decided 2026-07-16; simplified in re-review — D13):** a candidate
  and its stored partials are evicted together when the candidate's
  **commitment expires** (node's own clock). **Keyed by `commitment_id`; each
  distinct commitment is its own candidate — there is NO horizon extension**
  (a fresh commitment is a new key, a new candidate; the old one expires on its
  own clock). Pruning runs in the **same sweep the replay log already runs AND
  is enforced at `/channel` candidate lookup** (an idle node never runs the
  /sign-path sweep, so an expired candidate must be rejected on lookup too).
  **No armed/scheduled exemption in V0-8a** — V0-8a builds no arming, no timers,
  and no fire, so it can neither set nor clear such an exemption. The
  armed-candidate expiry exemption + its fire-complete cleanup are **V0-4/V0-8b
  work** (see scope guard), added where arming and firing actually live.
  *Tests: an expired candidate is gone after the sweep and a late partial for
  it is rejected as unknown/expired even with no intervening /sign; two live
  commitments over the same txid are two distinct candidates.*

### 5b. `/channel` response schema (codex audit — exact shapes + status mapping)
Every `/channel` POST returns one tagged JSON body `{ "status": <TAG>, ... }`
with a fixed HTTP status. Exactly four outcomes:
- **`ACCEPTED`** — HTTP 200 — `{"status":"ACCEPTED"}` — envelope verified and
  the partial stored (or an idempotent re-store of an already-verified partial).
- **`REJECTED`** — HTTP **400** — `{"status":"REJECTED","reason":"<code>"}` —
  **permanent, do NOT retry.** `reason` is a fixed enum whose exact variant
  names are frozen in the module table + tests (codex nit). An oversized
  `/channel` body returns tagged `REJECTED`/400 (not axum's untagged 413 — the
  channel surface is uniformly tagged; `/sign` keeps its existing 413).
  `send_partial` classifies `REJECTED` as permanent. The full mapping of
  every rejection branch (§3 ingress + §5 partial checks) to this response:
  malformed JSON, oversized body, bad `protocol_version`, wrong
  `recipient_node_id`, wrong `wallet_id`/`manifest_hash`, unknown
  `sender_node_id`, bad endorsement, bad `channel_sig`, stale/future
  `timestamp`, replayed `nonce`, malformed `payload_b64`, unknown `msg_type`,
  `signer_node_id != sender_node_id`, payload/envelope field mismatch, wrong
  descriptor pubkey / txid / input / sighash / `user_sig_hash`, bad partial
  signature — ALL map to `REJECTED` with a distinct `reason` code. (Body-size
  and JSON-parse failures may surface as the axum-standard 413/400 before the
  handler; document which, and keep it consistent.)
- **`UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`** — HTTP **409**, **retriable** —
  `{"status":"UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE"}` — envelope valid but the `commitment_id` is
  not (yet) a registered candidate here.
- **`RATE_LIMITED`** — HTTP **429**, retriable after backoff —
  `{"status":"RATE_LIMITED","retry_after_secs":<n>}` — per-peer quota or the
  pre-auth concurrency bound was hit.
Test the mapping: assert each rejection branch yields its exact status + reason.

### 6. Outbound: `send_partial` + bounded retry (reqwest)
- Add `reqwest` (default-tls off if unused; json feature as needed).
- `send_partial(peer, envelope)` POSTs to the peer's `/channel` with a
  per-send deadline and a bounded response read (`max_response_bytes`); a
  dead/unreachable peer is an error return, never a panic, and never blocks
  other sends (send to peers concurrently). Peer `endpoints` are canonical base
  URLs WITHOUT the `/channel` path; the sender appends `/channel` exactly once
  (codex nit).
- **Named bounded-retry helper (codex I1):** a `retry_partial_until` (or
  similar) that, on `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`/`RATE_LIMITED`, retries with backoff
  until the commitment expiry, then gives up. **CRITICAL (codex B1 fix
  2026-07-16): each retry RE-ENVELOPES from the immutable partial payload with a
  FRESH nonce + timestamp + `channel_sig`** — a channel nonce is single-use
  (consumed on the receiver at first sight), so re-sending the *same* envelope
  would self-reject as `REPLAYED_NONCE`. The helper holds the payload, not the
  envelope; it builds a new signed envelope per attempt. Tests: unknown-
  candidate → peer registers later → a freshly re-enveloped retry succeeds;
  **re-sending the identical envelope is rejected as replay, but a fresh
  re-envelope of the same payload is accepted** (prove both); expiry terminates
  retry; backoff honored; concurrent fan-out independent. One-shot
  `send_partial` alone is NOT sufficient.
- **Partial-release authorization (ADR-0012):** `send_partial` is
  `pub(crate)`, with the invariant documented at its definition: no partial
  may leave the node before its candidate's authorized fire event; V0-8a has
  NO production caller — V0-8b must add the fire-authorization gate before
  wiring one. Tests are the only callers in this task.

### 7. Signing-oracle prohibition (structural, absolute)
A peer message must **never** cause the node to create a signature. The
`/channel` handler only *verifies and stores*; it has structurally no path to
invoke the signer. Add a test asserting no channel message of any `msg_type`
triggers signing.

### 8. DoS guards (layered)
- **Pre-auth (cheap, before any crypto):** the existing 1 MiB body limit; a
  global bound on concurrent `/channel` requests — so forged traffic cannot
  burn a victim peer's quota or the node's CPU unboundedly.
- **Post-auth (after envelope verification):** per-peer quota
  (envelopes/minute) keyed by authenticated sender_node_id; duplicate-envelope
  suppression (the nonce set); the structural PartialStore bound from §5.
- Isolated from the watchtower task.

### 9. Module docs
Give the channel module a module-level ASCII diagram of the envelope ingress
pipeline (protocol_version → recipient bind → manifest → endorsement → sig →
freshness → nonce → decode payload_b64 → equality → candidate(commitment_id) →
verify-partial → store, with every rejection exit).

## Tests (`vault-node`)
- **Derivation**: channel key is a pure function — same config ⇒ same channel
  pubkey; channel pubkey ≠ signing pubkey.
- **Manifest/startup invariants**: a config whose signing key is not in the
  descriptor fails startup; manifest hash is stable across field-order
  permutations of the input (canonicalization works); endorsement over the
  wrong manifest_hash rejected.
- **Identity/endorsement**: endorsed by an in-manifest signing key → accepted;
  endorsed by a non-member key → rejected; **an envelope carrying another
  vault's `wallet_id`/`manifest_hash` → rejected by the direct local-equality
  check, independently of endorsement validity** (a well-formed envelope for a
  different vault is refused before sender lookup); **an envelope signed by the
  coordinator auth key instead of an endorsed channel key → rejected** (the
  "coordinator cannot mint a node" property, executable).
- **Envelope ingress rejection branches** (each its own test): tampered
  `payload_b64` bytes (channel_sig fails) → rejected; **`recipient_node_id` ≠
  my node_id → rejected** (cross-recipient replay); **`protocol_version` ≠
  manifest's → rejected**; stale timestamp → rejected; **future-stamped
  envelope's nonce retained until its timestamp leaves the window** (no ~60s
  replay reopen); replayed nonce → rejected AND the nonce set is pruned by
  timestamp (bounded); oversized body → rejected; per-peer quota exceeded →
  rejected; global concurrent bound enforced; malformed JSON → 400;
  payload/envelope field mismatch → rejected; `signer_node_id != sender_node_id`
  → rejected.
- **Wire preimage**: signature verifies over the raw `payload_b64` ASCII bytes
  WITHOUT decoding first (a valid envelope authenticates before any
  base64-decode); a bit-flip in `payload_b64` fails verification.
- **Partial exchange**: a valid partial over a registered candidate + correct
  descriptor pubkey verifies and is stored; wrong signer key, wrong txid,
  wrong input index, wrong sighash, wrong `user_sig_hash` → rejected;
  unknown-`commitment_id` → `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE` (retriable); duplicate
  suppressed; a second different partial for the same (candidate, input,
  signer) does not evict the first verified one.
- **Registry lifecycle**: two live commitments over the same txid (fresh
  nonce/expiry) are distinct candidates (keyed by `commitment_id`), and
  registering the second does not evict the first; each expires on its own
  commitment clock (no horizon extension); an expired candidate is rejected at
  `/channel` lookup with no intervening `/sign` sweep; at the hard capacity cap
  the new candidate is **not inserted** and no live candidate is evicted,
  **and the `/sign` verdict/response is unchanged by the cap** (capacity gates
  the registry slot, not the sign decision — no wire `AT_CAPACITY` in V0-8a).
- **Signing-oracle**: no channel message of any `msg_type` causes the node to
  produce a signature (assert the signer is never invoked from the channel
  path).
- **Outbound**: `send_partial` to a dead peer returns an error — no panic, no
  partial leaked, other peers still receive theirs (concurrent sends).
- **Two in-process nodes, through the REAL path:** each node receives the
  spend via `POST /sign` (registering the candidate), then exchanges one
  verified partial via `/channel` over loopback axum — no test-only injection
  of candidates.
- **Absent-channel mode**: a config with NO `[channel]` block starts, does not
  mount `/channel`, runs no manifest/bijection/endorsement assertions, and
  behaves as today — this is the mode `demo first-light` runs in. A config WITH
  `[channel]` mounts the route and enforces every invariant.
- **Config/startup**: endpoint mismatch (self entry vs actual bind) → fatal;
  a non-canonical/unparseable peer endpoint → fatal.
- **`/channel` response schema**: each rejection branch maps to exactly the
  right status (`REJECTED` permanent vs `UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE`/`RATE_LIMITED`
  retriable vs `ACCEPTED`).
- **Retry helper**: unknown-candidate → later registration → success; retry
  terminates at commitment expiry; backoff honored; concurrent fan-out
  independent.
- **Golden vectors**: each digest (channel-key, manifest hash, endorsement,
  envelope, user_sig_hash) verifies against a FIXED hard-coded vector.
- **Diagnostics**: freshness rejections surface through `/events` with peer
  attribution + monotonic count; saturated `/channel` load does not starve
  `/events` or the watchtower tick.
- `demo first-light` still exits 0 — it runs in **absent-channel mode** (no
  `[channel]` block; the demo is NOT edited; the channel is unused until V0-8b
  reworks the demo).

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-node/`, workspace `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` only.
  The ONLY `/sign`-path change is the `register_candidate` post-verdict funnel
  (§4) — a small behavior-preserving control-flow refactor, not literally one
  call site.
  Do NOT rework the coordinator or the demo (V0-8b). Do NOT build:
  combine/finalize/broadcast wiring (V0-8b), the duress state machine (V0-4),
  Tor or mTLS (v1), full manifest provisioning (V0-9), a
  leader/single-assembler (none is needed — the exchange is peer-to-peer),
  any session/connection state.
- **Explicit V0-8b/V0-4 obligations (recorded here so they are not lost):**
  (a) at ingress, refuse a hot-class spend whose commitment expiry < now +
  `hold_secs` + combine-slack (`EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT`) — under
  combine-at-Hold-expiry such a spend can never legally fire and must die
  loudly, not become a zombie candidate (V0-8b). (b) **Armed-candidate expiry
  exemption + fire-complete cleanup** (V0-4/V0-8b): a candidate that is
  armed/scheduled-to-fire must be exempt from the commitment-expiry sweep AND
  the `/channel`-lookup expiry rejection until its fire completes (an
  escape-class duress `T = first_seen + duress_delay_secs` can exceed
  `max_commitment_age_secs`, so plain expiry would delete the residual escape
  before T and kill the Firing job); the exemption needs a finite lifecycle
  (cleared on fire-complete) so it cannot pin the capacity cap. This is
  deferred OUT of V0-8a (D13) because V0-8a builds no arming/timer/fire to set
  or clear it. (c) **Capacity gate AFTER pin/safety** — once the safety track
  exists, evaluate the candidate-store capacity check after arm/freeze so a
  duress SpendRequest is never dropped for fullness (V0-4). (d) **At-capacity
  on an accepted verdict is a zombie** — a Pending spend accepted but not
  registered (store full) can never combine in V0-8b; surface/refuse it loudly
  at ingress rather than silently, per the `EXPIRY_TOO_SHORT` precedent
  (V0-8b/V0-4).
- Build the SIMPLEST correct thing that gives signed-envelope peer messaging +
  a verified partial exchange. Target ~1200–1600 lines is **advisory** (codex
  audit: with the full rejection matrix, golden vectors, retry tests, event
  changes, and the real-path E2E, ~1700–2300 is realistic) — **do NOT compress
  the wire contract, the rejection matrix, or the tests to hit a number, and do
  NOT stop merely because correct code crosses 1600 lines.** The size guard is
  against gold-plating/scope-creep, not against necessary coverage. If
  materially more, stop and simplify — but do not compress the wire contract
  or the rejection tests to hit the number.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- `nix develop -c cargo fmt --check`, `nix develop -c cargo clippy --workspace
  --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `nix develop -c cargo test --workspace` pass.
- `nix develop -c cargo run -p vault-cli -- demo first-light` exits 0.
- Channel identity is endorsement-verified against the manifest; every peer
  message proves possession via its envelope signature over canonical bytes;
  partials verify against the expected descriptor pubkey over the node's own
  REGISTERED sighash (candidate registry populated by the real `/sign` path)
  and are never blind-merged; no peer message can trigger signing; DoS guards
  are layered pre/post-auth and tested. The primitives are ready for V0-8b to
  drive combine + broadcast.


---
## Polish notes (bead-polish-loop 2026-07-16)
- **Intentionally ONE bead — do NOT split.** The channel is a tightly-coupled security surface: identity + manifest + envelope wire + candidate registry + partial exchange are exercised together by the two-node E2E, and splitting across PRs would merge half-channels that test nothing (and contradicts the eng-review decision to keep it one security-focused diff). Size (~1200-1600 lines) is expected; the scope guard's "stop and simplify if materially more" is the guard, not decomposition.
- **Authoritative design source (committed):** docs/adr/0012-model-b-spend-and-duress-architecture.md ("The node-to-node channel"), docs/adr/0013-concrete-protocol-schemas.md (§1 node_id order, §4 BaseManifest two-pass), docs/adr/0007-node-death-on-reboot.md (tmpfs), CONTEXT.md (glossary). These survived three two-model review rounds (commits 88561bf..e59157e). If this bead's spec and an ADR ever disagree, the ADR wins — reconcile before building.
- **Prerequisite:** btc-policy-a0i (axum migration) MUST be merged first (dependency in graph). Build on the async base.

## Second-model audit fixes folded (codex, 2026-07-16)
- Channel config is OPTIONAL (absent-channel mode) so demo first-light passes channel-less without editing the demo.
- Wire contract completed: all digest tags named, byte conventions fixed, /channel response schema (ACCEPTED/REJECTED/UNKNOWN_CANDIDATE/RATE_LIMITED), golden vectors required.
- Named bounded-retry helper with tests; diagnostics surface freshness rejections via /events; endpoint-consistency startup validation.
- NEW prerequisite: btc-policy-ykm (V0-2b, exact-tx commitment) — this bead now depends on BOTH a0i and ykm. commitment_id keying is unsafe until V0-2b binds version/nLockTime/nSequence.

## Final spec re-audit fixes folded (codex CONDITIONAL PASS → LAUNCH, 2026-07-16)
- B1 retry nonce: each retry re-envelopes the immutable payload with a fresh nonce/timestamp/sig; nonce consumed atomically after sig+freshness, keyed by authenticated sender.
- B2 byte-layout contradiction removed: length prefix only on variable fields; fixed-width numerics no prefix (node_id u16, protocol_version u32, timestamp u64); the "u64 for all numerics" wording retracted.
- B3 golden vectors: pin expected PREIMAGE BYTES (not just digests) + per-field envelope mutation tests (nonce/timestamp/msg_type each invalidate the sig) — closes common-mode omission.
- Startup: local channel-pubkey must equal self manifest entry; expected_manifest_hash compare.
- /channel oversized → tagged REJECTED/400 (not 413); REJECTED.reason variant names frozen.
- Preserve existing watchtower event JSON (generalize event enum) when adding freshness events.
- endpoints are base URLs; sender appends /channel once. Sizing ~1200-1600 is advisory (~1700-2300 realistic); do not compress tests.

title: Deliverable-5 out-of-lock /sign preflight concurrency hardening (9y5.3 follow-up)
description:
Follow-up from the 9y5.3 v0-exit multi-reviewer-loop (codex passes 3-6). The prevout preflight (deliverable 5) was hoisted OUT of sign_state to fix the round-2 P0 (under-lock chain I/O delaying Lockdown-at-T). That out-of-lock window surfaced three concurrency/ordering concerns, all degrading to frozen-funds -> recovery (NOT theft), deferred here rather than rushed as more crown-jewel surgery (each in-loop patch attempt introduced an ordering regression):

(A) REFRESH races a spend's preflight (codex): refresh subordination requires the spend in state.pending, but during the spend's out-of-lock preflight it is NOT yet registered, so a concurrent RefreshRequest can finish its own one-batch preflight, reacquire sign_state, see no pending spend, and register an immediately-fireable refresh. If it consumes an input the mandatory escape needs, it invalidates the escape even though the spend is later accepted -> the sweep can't cover -> recovery. Honest-reachable. Fix: an in-flight-spend subordination marker set BEFORE the preflight, cleared on EVERY exit, included in refresh subordination; pin-uniform + idempotent.

(B) STAGE / fan out before the chain preflight (codex): the duress self-hold + fanout (stage_spend_carrier) happens only AFTER the preflight, so a selectively-delivered carrier to a node whose backend hangs (<=120s) defers fanout+arming by that stall. The safety INTENT is already chain-independent (fire_arm_hook pre-preflight) and the refusal branches stage, so the stall is a bounded DELAY, not a miss; staging the FULL request before validation is invariant-blocked (it would propagate federation-uniform policy/mismatch refusals, breaking theft-recognition + silence). A correct fix needs a pin-uniform SAFETY-ONLY signal fanned out before the I/O, or a bounded stall.

(C) prevout FETCH-FAILURE propagation (reverted from 9y5.3 pass 5): forward a node-local backend-failure refusal so peers still process the carrier + the node self-holds (Fable pass-1). Must be done AFTER the accepted-replay lookup so a retry of an already-accepted request honours its cached ACCEPTED verdict instead of being overridden by a transient backend failure (codex pass-5 P1), and must distinguish node-local FETCH failure from federation-uniform value MISMATCH (the latter stays non-propagating). The hung-backend case is already handled in 9y5.3 (stall -> expiry -> node-local CommitmentExpired forward).

Acceptance: an in-flight spend subordinates concurrent refreshes across the preflight window (test: a refresh cannot invalidate an in-flight spend's escape); the duress fanout/arming does not depend on chain I/O without weakening don't-propagate-federation-uniform or silence; the fetch-failure refusal forwards correctly without overriding accepted-replay; fmt/clippy/test green; attack all still passes incl. a new spend-refresh-race scenario. Dep: 9y5.3.
close_reason: Out-of-lock /sign preflight concurrency hardening merged to main (f7ef28b). (A) in-flight-spend marker claimed under the phase-1 lock and RAII-released on every exit incl. panic unwind, consulted by refresh subordination — the mutex totally orders spend-vs-refresh so an in-flight spend is never invisible; (B) the duress fan-out's chain-I/O dependence is an explicitly bounded + tested stall, documented as covering the preflight only (not the phase-2 lock wait); (C) prevout fetch-failure forward re-landed AFTER the accepted-replay lookup, with node-local FETCH failure distinct from non-propagating federation-uniform MISMATCH, and the escape arm made exhaustive so a future Err variant cannot be swallowed. Preflight stays OUT of sign_state. Reviewed by codex (clean) + Fable. Gates: fmt/clippy-D/14 suites, attack 16/16, all 3 demos. SCOPE AMENDED EXPLICITLY: the 'attack all incl. spend-refresh-race scenario' line is not met — race proven deterministically at unit level with mock-backend barriers + code-verified ordering instead; a live version needs a deliberately stalled backend, the fragile pattern this bead's task file forbade (/healthz over-spec lesson). Filed as btc-policy-6nv with the untested residual (real HTTP threading, real lock contention) recorded.

title: Freeze one auditable release: reproducible signed binaries + dependency gates + recorded matrix
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (codex #4, and the remaining automatable half of btc-policy-9y5.8 deliverable 2).

WHY: there is no way today for an operator — or an auditor — to verify that a binary corresponds to a given commit. That matters beyond hygiene: 'reproducible builds' is one of the TWO stated mitigations for ADR-0012's pre-wrench coordinator compromise, the only accepted CONDITIONAL-THEFT residual in the threat model (R8b). It is currently mitigated by a paragraph. The other stated mitigation, a hardened dedicated coordinator host, is also unbuilt.

Also: docs/SIGNET-SPEND-RECORD.md records DEBUG binaries at commit 6c04bad, and main is now thousands of lines further on across the same chain-tracking and concurrency paths. That record is explicitly NOT evidence about main (staleness note added in 14c2312).

DELIVER: (a) a reproducible build — pinned toolchain, deterministic flags, documented procedure — such that an independent rebuild of a given commit yields byte-identical binaries, verified by someone rebuilding on a DIFFERENT machine (a hash produced by the same box proves nothing); (b) signed release artifacts; (c) cargo audit / cargo deny wired into CI, the gap docs/SBOM-AND-DEPENDENCY-POLICY.md already admits; (d) the FULL matrix run against that frozen commit with recorded toolchain/binary-hash/config/harness artifacts, including the V0-7 proptest+fuzz suites; (e) a FRESH signet spend against those exact binaries, regenerating SIGNET-SPEND-RECORD.md at that commit.

WHY IT GATES THE AUDIT: an external reviewer should review a frozen target, not a moving branch. Both reviewers said so independently.

VERIFY: two machines produce identical hashes; CI fails on a known-vulnerable dependency; the recorded matrix and the signet record both name the same commit and the same binary hashes.

title: V0-10: recovery-path branch + recovery spend
description:
## V0-10: recovery-path branch older(4224679) (BIP68 time-flag|30375 units) + node descriptor-parse + watchtower recovery recognition + MTP-matured recovery spend. Audit-clean (r4).

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file gitignored):

# V0-10: recovery-path descriptor branch + recovery spend construction

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- Surfaced by the 2026-07-17 spine audit as a prerequisite for V0-4b's
  "freeze + lockdown → recovery" claim: the current first-light descriptor has
  NO recovery branch, so a locked-down vault has no demonstrable exit.
  Authoritative: `docs/DESIGN.md` (recovery: Liana pattern, per-vault timelock,
  2-of-3 recovery keyset, 180-day default), `docs/adr/0013-...` §1 (the
  `wsh(...)` template: normal branch `USER + thresh(node keys)` OR recovery
  branch `older(TIMELOCK) + 2-of-3 recovery keys`; BIP68 512-sec units, 180d =
  30375), `CONTEXT.md` (Recovery path, Recovery keyset).

## Outcome
The vault descriptor gains its **recovery branch** — `older(TIMELOCK)` +
a 2-of-3 recovery keyset — and the CLI can construct + broadcast a recovery-path
spend once the relative timelock matures. This is the exit a locked-down or
otherwise-stuck vault takes: after the timelock, the recovery keys move funds
without the normal path (no node quorum, no coordinator). It makes V0-4b's
"funds frozen → recovery" a demonstrable outcome, not a claim.

## Why this exists
V0-4b's whole safety story is "freeze + lockdown → recovery": the sweep may
fail, funds sit frozen, and the user exits via the timelocked recovery path.
Until the recovery branch exists and a recovery spend can be built + confirmed on
regtest, that exit is unbuilt and V0-4b cannot demonstrate its safety property.

## Required changes (`crates/policy-core`, `crates/vault-node`, `crates/vault-cli`, descriptor/config)
1. **Descriptor recovery branch (ADR-0013 §1):** the vault `wsh(...)` template
   becomes `normal-branch OR recovery-branch` where recovery =
   `older(4224679) + thresh(2, <3 recovery keys>)`. **BIP68 encoding (codex fix
   2026-07-17): rust-miniscript's `older(n)` uses `n` as the RAW consensus
   `nSequence` value and does NOT add the time-flag automatically.** A 180-day
   TIME-based relative lock is `30375` units of 512s (180d = ⌈180·86400/512⌉),
   and the raw nSequence with the BIP68 type-flag (bit 22) set is
   `30375 | (1 << 22) = 4224679 = 0x004076a7`. So **the frozen descriptor
   contains `older(4224679)`** (NOT `older(30375)`, which is a 30375-BLOCK
   height lock — the wrong policy). Construct it via
   `Sequence::from_512_second_intervals(30375)` /
   `RelLockTime::from_512_second_intervals(30375)` and assert the compiled value
   equals `4224679` (time-flag set, 30375 units). **ADR-0013 §1 gets the same
   correction** (its "stores 30375" is the unit count; the descriptor arg is the
   raw 4224679). The demo vault gains a recovery keyset (throwaway regtest keys).
   Setup still rejects any descriptor outside the template.
2. **Node-side descriptor parse + watchtower recognition (codex fix — was wrongly
   excluded):** every node now parses the TWO-branch descriptor at startup
   without failing; and the V0-6/6b watchtower must classify a recovery-branch
   spend as `RecoveryPathSpend` (branch-identifiable on-chain), NOT
   `UnrecognizedSpend`. This is node-side work (`crates/vault-node`), required so
   the new descriptor does not break startup or misclassify the recovery spend.
3. **Recovery spend construction (`vault-cli`):** build a recovery-path spend
   (spends vault UTXOs via the recovery branch: sets the BIP68 time-unit
   relative-lock `nSequence`, 2-of-3 recovery signatures) and broadcast it. On
   regtest, **advance MEDIAN-TIME-PAST past the 512-sec-unit relative lock**
   (`setmocktime` + mining blocks with advancing timestamps — NOT mining 30375
   blocks; a time-unit BIP68 lock matures on MTP, not height), so it confirms. A
   recovery spend attempted BEFORE MTP matures the lock is consensus-rejected
   (non-BIP68-final) — test that too.
4. **Recovery is the FALLBACK exit, not the first-line attack response**
   (codex wording fix): attacks are answered by the normal path + the escape
   sweep; recovery is the exit taken AFTER a failed escape + terminal lockdown,
   and for loss/inheritance/stuck-vault. Document with that precision (the old
   "not the answer to an attack" wording conflicted with its lockdown-after-
   attack purpose).

## Tests
- The descriptor compiles to the template with both branches; the compiled
  recovery `nSequence` carries the **BIP68 time-unit flag** (512-sec units), not
  a block-count lock; setup accepts it; a descriptor missing the recovery branch
  or with the wrong shape → rejected.
- **Every node parses the two-branch descriptor at startup** without failing
  (node-side).
- A recovery spend before the relative lock matures (by MTP) → consensus-rejected
  (non-BIP68-final); after **advancing median-time-past** past the 512-sec-unit
  lock (`setmocktime`, NOT mining 30375 blocks) → confirms.
- The watchtower classifies a recovery-path spend as `RecoveryPathSpend` (not
  `UnrecognizedSpend`) and alerts.
- 2-of-3 recovery signatures required (1-of-3 insufficient).
- `demo first-light` exits 0 (recovery branch present, unused on the normal
  path); optionally a `demo recovery-drill` act exercising the MTP-matured
  recovery spend.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/policy-core/` (descriptor template), `crates/vault-node/`
  (two-branch descriptor parse at startup + watchtower recovery-branch
  classification), `crates/vault-cli/` (recovery construction + demo),
  descriptor/config. Do NOT build duress (V0-4), the Model-B combine path
  (V0-8b), or inheritance/multi-user key ceremonies.
- Non-goals: recovery key backup UX, social recovery, dynamic timelock. Build the
  simplest correct timelocked recovery branch + spend.
- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,
  `.ralph-burning/`, `.git/ralph-burning-live/`, `.beads/`.

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- The vault descriptor has the `older(4224679) + 2-of-3` recovery branch (BIP68
  time-based, 30375 units of 512s + type-flag bit 22); a
  recovery spend confirms only after the relative timelock matures; the
  watchtower alerts on it. V0-4b can now demonstrate "funds frozen → recovery".

title: vault-node: replace the startup scantxoutset UTXO warm with descriptor-wallet tracking
description: REAL-CHAIN FINDING from the 9y5.8 signet spend (docs/SIGNET-SPEND-RECORD.md). The node's startup vault-unspent warm (and the periodic refresh) issues a FULL scantxoutset. On signet's 72,273,640-output UTXO set that costs ~10.4s per scan, and Bitcoin Core serializes scans PROCESS-WIDE — so five nodes sharing one backend queue their scans behind each other and later nodes exceed a 15s readiness deadline. Gates: fmt/clippy-D/workspace tests, attack 16/16, all 3 demos, plus a signet re-run showing node boot without the sequential workaround.

title: Independent federation runtime: five hosts, authenticated transport, enforced correlation diversity
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (codex #1, the single most fundamental gap; both reviewers named the host as their first attack target).

WHY: docs/SETUP-CEREMONY.md provisions five vault-node PROCESSES ON ONE HOST, and the channel endpoints are hard-wired loopback (crates/vault-node/src/channel.rs ~2934). ADR-0009 requires that no correlation class (host, OS, provider, operator, location) reach quorum — one host IS a correlation class holding ALL FIVE node signing keys. So 3-of-5 is today a property of the DESIGN, not of the DEPLOYMENT. An attacker who takes that host reads five keys from process memory, adds the user key or one coerced signature, and produces a direct on-chain witness: PIN, allowlist, Hold, duress, watchtower and the release gate are all off-chain policy and none of them apply once the keys are held. Every other hardening in this repo is downstream of this being false.

DELIVER: (a) five genuinely independent hosts, each with its OWN chain backend; (b) authenticated, routable node-to-node transport (not loopback) — ADR-0011's channel over a real network, with the manifest-pinned endpoints and channel-key endorsements doing the work they were designed for; (c) deploy-time enforcement/attestation of correlation diversity, so a misprovisioned federation FAILS rather than silently collapsing to one class; (d) an honest statement of what diversity is actually achieved (provider, region, OS, operator) — ADR-0009 is only as true as the deployment makes it.

NON-GOALS: Tor/mTLS hardening beyond what authenticated transport needs (separate work); changing the protocol; changing the ceremony's key-independence checks.

CARE: the per-link partition attack explicitly accepted at channel.rs ~3580 (arm one node while an unfrozen quorum remains) is currently tolerable because all links are loopback on one box. On real links it is a live attack surface and must be re-analysed, not inherited.

VERIFY: a federation on five separate hosts completes an honest spend, a clawback, and a duress arm+Lockdown; a deliberately misprovisioned (co-located) federation is REFUSED at deploy time; the partition analysis is redone for real links.

title: Operator CLI: spend / refresh / pending / escape / recover against a SEALED vault
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (Fable #1). VERIFIED: crates/vault-cli/src/main.rs exposes only setup, demo, attack, and 'signet spend'. NOTHING outside setup.rs reads manifest.json (zero hits workspace-wide). Every driver — demo, attack, signet spend — builds its federation IN-PROCESS with ephemeral Actor::random user/hot/escape/coordinator keys (e.g. crates/vault-cli/src/signet.rs ~152).

WHY: 'setup finalize' writes a descriptor, manifest.json, and coordinator-auth.secret that NO CODE IN THIS REPOSITORY CAN CONSUME. A user can seal a real vault and then cannot spend from it, refresh it, claw back during a Hold, or drive recovery. docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md §6 instructs a user under attack to 'submit an escape-class spend under the normal PIN' — with a tool that does not exist; §1 tells them to poll /pending, presumably by hand. The runbook documents a system one layer more finished than the one built (now recorded as threat-model R9). This is why the product does not exist yet, independent of how good the protocol core is.

DELIVER a real coordinator CLI that LOADS A SEALED MANIFEST (manifest.json + descriptor + coordinator-auth.secret) and drives the live federation over HTTP: 'spend' (compose spend + mandatory escape + fee-bump ladder, user-sign, coord-authenticate, relay, watch), 'refresh' (the first-class pin-less refresh — WITHOUT it the 180-day recovery branch matures and stolen recovery keys win, a residual ADR-0012 quietly assumes away), 'pending' (poll every node's GET /pending and diff against the spends the user authorized — the incident surface btc-policy-k0t built), 'escape' (the clawback the runbook already tells users to perform), and 'recover' (drive the 2-of-3 timelocked branch).

CONSTRAINTS: the coordinator stays an UNTRUSTED RELAY (ADR-0010) — it must never gain a signing capability, must never broadcast (nodes broadcast; vault-cli's zero-sendrawtransaction property is asserted by the demos and must hold here), and must not weaken SILENCE by displaying anything pin-dependent. The user key must be supplied through the hardware-signing seam (btc-policy-hwk), not embedded.

NON-GOALS: a GUI; a daemon; monitoring/alerting integration; changing node-side protocol.

VERIFY: an END-TO-END test that crosses the seal->operate seam — 'setup finalize' output is consumed by the CLI to complete an honest spend on regtest. That seam is currently untested by ANY gate, which is why 657 passing tests and attack 16/16 coexist with an unusable product.

title: Resolve the node lifecycle contradiction, then destructively drill it
description:
FROM THE 2026-07-29 STATE REVIEW (codex #2). The operational documents are MUTUALLY INCOMPATIBLE, which means routine maintenance has no valid security-preserving procedure:
 - ADR-0005: the host is SEALED — SSH uninstalled, no administrative access path, 'no reset, no reconfiguration, no upgrade-in-place'.
 - ADR-0007: a rebooted node is a DEAD node (tmpfs; the reboot wipes key, Lockdown latch, generation marker).
 - docs/SETUP-CEREMONY.md: each node starts once and its preimage is destroyed.
 - docs/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md: every start needs the preimage, and it is a backup item.
(The rolling-restart claim in UPGRADE-AND-ROTATION-POLICY was already deleted in 14c2312 as unperformable under ADR-0005; this bead resolves the REMAINING tension rather than papering it.)

DECIDE, in an ADR, ONE model:
 (a) immutable one-shot nodes — every binary or config change is a vault migration, the preimage is genuinely destroyed after first start, and there is no supported restart; or
 (b) recoverable hardware-backed nodes — the signing key lives in hardware rather than being re-derived from an operator preimage, restart is a supported operation, and Lockdown becomes a DURABLE MONOTONIC latch rather than something a reboot clears.
Option (b) is the one codex recommends longer-term; option (a) is what the code implements today. Whichever is chosen, the ADR must supersede or amend the losers explicitly — this failure mode is documents disagreeing, so a new document that merely adds a fourth voice makes it worse.

THEN DRILL IT DESTRUCTIVELY, because 'a backup you have never restored from is a hypothesis' (OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK §7) applies to this entire layer: reboot a node; restore from backup; lose quorum and recover; migrate a vault end-to-end; drive the 2-of-3 recovery branch from cold artifacts ALONE (descriptor + manifest + recovery keys, no live federation). Record what actually happened, including what broke.

VERIFY: the drill is reproducible and its results are recorded; every operational doc points at the same model; no procedure remains that a sealed node cannot perform.

title: V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest demonstration
description:
## V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest harness demonstrating the duress mechanism on a live n=2t-1 federation. Split from V0-4b-core per the 2026-07-17 audit so a security invariant is not split across implementations. UPDATED 2026-07-20 to the mechanism the dual-model review settled: the signer/partial COUPLING + RELEASE-GATE is the theft proof (not the t-holder receipt count, which is timing), and the one residual (duress-signal censorship of a pre-pending normal hot spend from a sub-quorum) is BOUNDED by the V0-11 Hot budget (ADR-0014). Scenarios: toxic-parent, in-flight-refresh, two-spend-probe(silence), escape+refresh, arm-split-closed(coupling), censorship-residual-bounded(hot budget), partition, reboot-death, coverage/feerate fire-failure, recovery.

FULL TASK SPEC (self-contained; source task file .rb-lite/tasks/v0-4b-harness-adversarial.md is gitignored):

# V0-4b-harness: adversarial regtest harness for the duress mechanism

## Environment — read first
- No system C compiler. Run cargo/bitcoind via `nix develop -c ...`.
- **Prerequisite merged:** V0-4b-core (the two-track duress state machine) + the
  V0-11 hot-spend bound — plus everything they consume (V0-8b, V0-4a, V0-10).
  This bead is the **launch-gate adversarial demonstration**, split from the core
  per the 2026-07-17 audit so a security invariant is not split across
  implementations: the core owns the production state machine + its unit/model
  tests; this owns the broad, environment-heavy regtest/CLI scenarios.
- Authoritative for the MECHANISM (read before writing a single assertion):
  - `docs/adr/0012-...` — the two-track state machine, the transition table, and
    the invariant list. **Two passages are load-bearing and were re-settled by the
    2026-07-20 dual-model (codex + Fable) review; the harness must assert the
    property they state, not the earlier one:**
    - the **"CORRECTION (2026-07-20)"** paragraph at the end of the §"Duress state
      machine" intro, and
    - the **"Partial-release authorization (both candidates)"** invariant (the
      release-gate).
  - `docs/adr/0014-hot-spend-bound.md` — the Hot budget (per-tx cap + velocity
    ledger) that BOUNDS the one residual this design leaves open.
  - `docs/DESIGN.md` (Success Criteria; attack scenarios), `CONTEXT.md`
    ("Duress PIN", "Hot budget").

## The mechanism this harness demonstrates (assert THIS, not the count)
The safety property is **not** "t nodes armed." With `n = 2t−1` and up to `t−1`
compromised, a holder set of size `t` has only `≥ 1` honest member, so a receipt
count can never *prove* `t` honest nodes froze — a receipt proves relay, not
freeze. The confirmation count is a **timing/liveness** mechanism (when the
freeze/sweep commit), not the theft proof.

What makes a coerced spend un-completable is the **signer/partial coupling +
release-gate** (ADR-0012 "Partial-release authorization" + the signing-oracle
prohibition):
1. **Coupling.** A node emits a partial for a candidate ONLY after independently
   receiving and processing that candidate's own user-authorized carrier (no
   peer message is ever a signing oracle). Processing a **duress**-pin carrier
   arms → freezes that candidate under the same store lock that would release it.
   So the set of honest nodes that hold a *releasable* partial for a
   duress-carried spend is a subset of the set that *froze* it — you cannot have
   an honest node that signed the carrier but did not freeze it. The arm cannot
   be split away from the signature.
2. **Release-gate.** Neither the spend's nor the escape's partial leaves the node
   before that candidate's authorized fire event; arming atomically + monotonically
   suppresses every existing and future hot-partial release. A hot candidate is
   never observable open-but-unfrozen (the freeze is set under the release lock).
3. **Result.** No honest node ever releases a coerced partial → only `≤ t−1`
   compromised nodes can → never a signing quorum. The sweep may still fail
   (funds sit frozen → recovery); that is denial, never theft.

**The one residual, and its bound.** A DIFFERENT case is not closed by the
coupling: a hot spend submitted EARLIER with the *normal* pin (legitimately
pending in Hold, every node holding an unfrozen partial), where a later duress
signal is **censored by a compromised coordinator** from a sub-quorum of honest
nodes — those nodes never freeze it and release at Hold-expiry. This censorship
residual is the accepted "hot wallet is the risk budget" residual, and it is
**bounded** by the V0-11 Hot budget (per-tx cap + rolling-window velocity), so
the most it can admit per window is one Hot budget, never the vault (ADR-0014).

## Outcome
An adversarial regtest harness (a `vault-cli attack`/`demo` subcommand and/or an
integration-test module) that DEMONSTRATES, end-to-end on a live regtest
federation (`n = 2t−1`, e.g. 3-of-5), that the duress mechanism holds its safety +
silence properties under adversarial conditions: freeze + lockdown → recovery, no
theft path, silent to an outside attacker, and the censorship residual empirically
bounded to the Hot budget. This is the empirical counterpart to V0-4b-core's unit
tests — the "wrench-attack answer is live" evidence.

## Why this exists
ADR-0012 says several duress properties are best "verified empirically … with an
adversarial regtest harness" — they involve process kills, network partitions,
mempool packages, and timing probes that unit tests can't fully exercise. And the
2026-07-20 review turned on a mechanism (coupling + release-gate vs. a receipt
count) that a live demonstration must pin down: the harness proves the *coupling*
holds against a coordinator that actively tries to split the arm from the
signature, and that the residual it does not close is bounded by the Hot budget.

## Required — the harness scenarios (each asserts the SAFETY outcome + no theft)
1. **toxic-parent**: an escape built over an external unconfirmed deposit →
   excluded (build-over-mempool); the escape either fires over vault-authorized
   inputs only or the sweep fails → Lockdown → recovery. No poisoned escape.
2. **in-flight-refresh**: a refresh in flight when duress arms → the escape
   chains off the refresh output (vault-authorized) OR the sweep fails → denial,
   never theft; the coerced hot spend is dead (frozen partial + unconditional
   Lockdown at T).
3. **two-spend-probe (silence)**: an attacker probing with two spends cannot read
   the duress bit — identical observable outcomes (latency, `/events`, peer
   traffic, response size) under both pins. Include the Hot-budget refusal path:
   a `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` refusal is pin-independent, so it does not leak the bit.
4. **escape-class + refresh sequences**: the two-slot record + `Idle→Armed`
   suppression behave per the transition table; escape-class completes + residual
   sweep over disjoint/union inputs; the normal pin's delayed slot is a no-op.
5. **arm-split-closed (the coupling — codex P0, 2026-07-19)**: a coerced hot spend
   submitted WITH the duress pin; a compromised coordinator tries to split the arm
   from the signature by making the carrier reach exactly ONE honest node and not
   the rest, via each concrete vector ADR-0012 names: (a) corrupt the user-signed
   escape so a peer's local policy refuses before propagation, (b) oversize the
   carrier past a peer's `max_msg_bytes`, (c) set an expiry that lapses mid-fan-out.
   **Assert the coupling, not a count:** the honest nodes that did not receive the
   carrier never signed its partial (no signing oracle), and the one(s) that did
   receive it froze it (release-gate). So at Hold-expiry the releasable partials
   number `≤ t−1` (compromised only) → the combine cannot reach a quorum → the
   coerced spend never broadcasts. Lockdown at T on the armed node(s) → recovery.
   There is no honest node that signed the carrier but left its partial unfrozen.
6. **censorship-residual-bounded (the Hot budget — ADR-0014 / V0-11)**: the case
   the coupling does NOT close — a hot spend pending under the *normal* pin, with a
   later duress signal censored from a sub-quorum. Demonstrate the BOUND, three
   parts: (a) an over-`hot_max_per_tx` coerced hot spend is refused at ingress at
   EVERY node with `HOT_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` **before signing**, so it never becomes a
   censor-completable pending candidate — and the duress arm still fires +
   propagates on that refusal path (composition); (b) within-cap hot spends whose
   window sum exceeds `hot_max_per_window` hit `HOT_VELOCITY_EXCEEDED` at ingress on
   the 2nd+ (an attacker cannot queue several large hot spends in one Hold and clear
   them all); (c) the release path gives budget back — a hot spend cancelled/expired
   **while still unexposed** frees its reservation, while a broadcast/released one
   meters to age-out (monotonic window). Net: the censored-completion is bounded to
   ≤ one window's Hot budget, never the vault.
7. **partition / selective delivery**: deliver the duress carrier to a subset of
   nodes. Safety does **not** depend on every node arming; it depends on the
   coupling — assert no honest node releases a coerced partial regardless of how
   many armed. Drop the reachable-armed set below `t` → lockdown-only (no sweep, no
   theft) → recovery. (Contrast with the OLD framing "propagation arms every
   reachable node": that all-or-nothing arming is the timing story, not the safety.)
8. **process-kill / reboot-death**: kill an armed node (destroy its tmpfs
   deployment) before T → surviving armed set (≥ t) still fires the sweep; drop
   below t → lockdown-only; the killed node holds no keys/schedule/partials and
   cannot restart/rejoin (RAMDISK reboot-death). Also cover the lockdown latch
   surviving a PROCESS restart but dying on machine reboot (V0-4a durability).
9. **coverage/feerate/package fire-time failures** on live regtest → the sweep
   does not fire, Lockdown at T still happens (unconditional), funds recoverable
   via V0-10.
10. **recovery demonstration**: after a lockdown-only outcome, exercise the V0-10
    timelocked recovery spend (time-warp past the relative lock) → funds move via
    recovery. This makes "freeze + lockdown → recovery" a demonstrated exit.

## Tests / acceptance
- Each scenario runs on a co-located regtest federation (`n = 2t−1`) and asserts:
  no theft path (funds only ever reach vault/hot/escape/recovery, never an attacker
  address the user didn't author), the SAFETY track held (freeze + unconditional
  Lockdown at T), and — for the probe/timing scenarios — silence (indistinguishable
  observables under both pins, including the Hot-budget refusal path).
- The arm-split scenario asserts the **coupling** specifically: enumerate the
  honest nodes that emitted a partial for the coerced carrier and show every one of
  them also froze it (releasable-partial count ≤ t−1). A test that only counts
  "how many armed" is asserting the wrong property — it must show no signed-but-
  unfrozen honest partial exists.
- The Hot-budget scenario asserts the numeric bound: over-cap refused pre-signing
  at every node; window sum capped; released/expired reservations returned.
- A scorecard-style exit (like `demo first-light`) communicates pass/fail per
  scenario; the whole harness exits 0 when all safety assertions hold.
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` still exits 0.

## Scope guard
- Touch `crates/vault-cli/` (attack/demo subcommand) + integration test modules;
  MINIMAL `crates/vault-node/` changes only if a test seam is genuinely needed
  (prefer driving the real daemon). Do NOT change the duress state machine
  (V0-4b-core), the channel, the release-gate, policy, or the Hot budget ledger —
  DRIVE them adversarially. If a scenario cannot be demonstrated without changing
  production safety code, STOP and flag it rather than weakening the mechanism to
  make a test pass.
- Non-goals: multi-VPS attack range (Approach B, later), the full v1 nine-scenario
  playbook — build the ADR-0012 denial-residual set + the coupling (arm-split) +
  the Hot-budget bound + reboot-death + recovery demonstration. No new production
  safety mechanism; no durable ledger (RAMDISK only). Size budget: a bounded

- Do not run `rb-lite`, signal your own process tree, or touch `.rb-lite/`,

## Acceptance criteria
- fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace pass; `demo first-light` exits 0.
- The harness demonstrates, on live regtest (`n = 2t−1`), freeze+lockdown→recovery

  (the censorship residual capped to one window's budget, refused pre-signing);
  reboot-death; and recovery. The wrench-attack answer is empirically demonstrated,
  and it demonstrates the mechanism the 2026-07-20 review settled — the release-gate
